news.originalContent: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities.   Follow Ynetnews on Facebook and Twitter >> Related stories: Israel names two sisters killed in West Bank terror attack At least one dead and six injured in a terror attack in Tel Aviv Family loses two daughters to deadly terror attack Members of the Jewish London community, including friends of the family, who heard of the devastating news after the Shabbat ended, were confronted only then, with the horrific reports of Maia and Rina's death. The funerals for the Dee sisters will be held today at the Kfar Etzion Cemetery.   Rabbi Leo Dee served as the Assistant Rabbi at the Hendon United Synagogue in North London from 2008-2011, and as the Senior Rabbi at Radlett United Synagogue from 2011-2014, after which the family made aliyah. They were a much beloved and respected family in the UK Jewish community. “People feel shock and disappointment. The family were communal people and served their communities well and were well-liked.” said a former member of the congregation at Hendon United Synagogue who did not wish to be named.  “I feel sick seeing this… good people who would never hurt anyone, murdered. I can't imagine his anguish, and pray Lucy survives,” said Joseph, another former congregant.   Chief UK Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis laments the death of the British-Israeli girls murdered in Friday's terror strike on the West Bank.  In a statement, the rabbi said: "No words can describe the depth of our shock and sadness at the heartbreaking news of the murder by terrorists in Israel of Maya & Rina Dee, daughters of Rebbetzen Lucy, who is in a critical condition & Rabbi Leo Dee, my dear colleagues. He continued, “They were much loved in the Hendon and Radlett communities in the UK, as well as in Israel and well beyond.” UK statement not mentioning terrorism The British Board of Deputies also issued a statement expressing shock over the tragic attack: “We are deeply shocked and saddened at the murder by Palestinian terrorists of Maia and Rina Dee, the daughters of Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee formerly of Radlett United Synagogue. We wish Lucy Refuah Shlemah and long life to the family as they cope with this devastating news.” Palestinian terrorist shot and killed 2 British-Israeli nationals, also critically injuring their mother in the West Bank. The victims were identified Saturday as 15-year-old Rina Dee and 20-year-old Maia Dee, the daughters of British-born Rabbi Leo Dee.  While their mother, Lucy (Lea), remains in critical condition fighting for her life, the Jewish community in the UK has expressed shock and sorrow at the brutal act of terrorism against former members of their community.    While many Jewish community leaders spoke out about the attack, the UK government has received criticism from some members of the community for its weakly-worded response to the killing of two of its own citizens.  One member of the Jewish community told Ynet that it was shocking that the UK statement didn’t even mention terrorism. “The response would be different if this happened elsewhere in the world. There is a double standard for British people killed in Israel,” he said.  The UK’s official statement read: “We are saddened to hear about the deaths of two British-Israeli citizens and the serious injuries sustained by a third individual. The UK calls for all parties across the region to de-escalate tensions.” "Tragedy for global Jewish community" Avi Abelow, family friend, said Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee are beloved and active members of their community in Efrat. "Two of the sweetest people with the sweetest children", he added. "Rabbi Leo continues to teach Torah classes in his Efrat synagogue today. All the youth of Efrat, as their families, are mourning the loss of either their personal friend or the sibling of their personal friend."  He mentioned that "Just last night the whole community got together, including many youth, for a special communal prayer gathering to pray for Lucy's recovery. The brutal Arab Muslim terrorist attack that murdered these two young, innocent Jewish women, and seriously injured their mother fighting for her life, is not just a tragedy for their family, but for the whole Efrat community and the global Jewish community.  "At the same time that another terrorist committed a terror attack in Tel Aviv, which killed an Italian tourist, and terrorist organizations are shooting rockets at Israel from Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, we are once again reminded that the Jewish people have enemies trying to kill us everywhere in our country for just being Jews living in our ancestral homeland.  "If only the UK government and other global bodies would recognize this truth, and truly give support to Israel to stop this ongoing terror war against Israel, which causes loss of life for everyone. In the meantime, as a personal friend and neighbor of the Dee family, my family, neighbors, and community will continue to assist and comfort the Dee family, as we assisted and comforted the family of our other friend and neighbor, Ari Fuld, murdered by terrorists back in 2018."

news.originalTitle: Iran's Guards warn protesters of 'decisive' action if unrest continues
news.title: Iran's Guards warn protesters of 'decisive' action if unrest continues
news.originalSummary: Iran's powerful Revolutionary Guards warned anti-government protesters of "decisive" action if unrest over gasoline price hikes do not cease, state television reported on Monday. A federal grand jury indicted the leaders of a powerful Mexican drug cartel and 19 others Wednesday, accusing them of a range of crimes, including drug trafficking and smuggling firearms from the US into Mexico.

The indictment accuses Mexican nationals Johnny Hurtado Olascoaga, alias “El Pez,” and Jose Alfredo Hurtado Olascoaga, alias “El Fresa,” of leading La Nueva Familia Michoacana cartel.

The two are currently at large.

La Nueva Familia Michoacana, or LNFM, is one of nearly two dozen Latin American and Caribbean gangs designated by the Trump administration as a foreign terrorist organization.

The cartel, founded in 2006, operates in the Mexican states of Michoacan and Guerrero, and authorities say it produces and distributes drugs. The brothers took control of the cartel in 2011.

The brothers are charged with conspiring to distribute and import cocaine, heroin and methamphetamine, trafficking firearms — including .50-caliber rifles — international money laundering and human smuggling.

The brothers, along with 14 others accused in the case, are at large and believed to be in Mexico, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Texas.

The US is offering rewards of $5 million and $3 million for information leading to the brothers’ capture.

The indictment, which was filed in federal court in Western Texas, also accuses 19 others of being members and associates of the cartel and committing related crimes.

All 21 are charged with racketeering.

The cartel uses violence, extortion and bribery to maintain its criminal operations, authorities said.

Edgar Aguilar Cruz of Mexico, for instance, orchestrated the purchase of firearms “by numerous straw purchasers throughout Texas and the Southeastern United States,” according to the indictment.

The guns were eventually transported to Mexico by couriers.

He is also accused of overseeing the cartel’s for-profit human smuggling operations, which transport people across the US-Mexico border and within the US.

US citizens are among the accused, including a 23-year-old man who is alleged to have been a “mid-level drug trafficker who coordinates drug trafficking logistics” for the cartel, primarily in Texas and North Carolina.

Another US citizen, a 35-year-old man, recruited people to buy firearms for the cartel, authorities said.

Cash profits from drug trafficking and human smuggling were often transported together with firearms back to the cartel in Mexico, according to the indictment.

Members and associates of the cartel discussed obtaining military-grade weapons, such as rocket-propelled grenades, and cartel leaders customized their guns with gold plating and cartoon and religious figures, authorities said.

Only five of the accused are in federal custody, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Texas. Gregory Torres, an attorney for Rogelio Ponce Esquivel, a 33-year-old Mexican national who is charged in the indictment and is in custody, declined to comment. It is unclear if the other four who were detained have lawyers.

In addition to its drug and firearm trafficking and human smuggling operations, the cartel has expanded to control mines and barter with Chinese companies to trade Mexican minerals for chemicals used in drug distribution, the indictment said.

news.originalSummary:
Train collides with minibus in Indonesia

Dramatic footage shows a passenger train pushing a flaming minibus along the tracks after colliding with it at a railway crossing in North Sumatra, Indonesia. Three crew members were injured and taken to hospital. The collision temporarily halted rail services.

As a man in Louisiana prepares to stand trial next month for the alleged rape of a Louisiana State University student who was later struck and killed by a car, court documents show he sent a series of frantic text messages about his mother’s instructions to stay quiet.

Rape suspects in LSU student Madison Brooks’ death want to keep texts out of trial

Madison Brooks, a 19-year-old LSU student at the time, was allegedly gang-raped by a group of men after a night out at a bar near the Baton Rouge campus in 2023, then struck and killed by a car.

Her blood alcohol concentration was 0.319% at the time of her death, nearly four times Louisiana’s legal driving limit for adults 21 and older.

Desmond Carter, 21, one of several men charged in connection with Brooks’ alleged rape, exchanged a series of text messages with co-defendants Casen Carver and Kaivon Washington, repeatedly saying that his mother had warned him not to speak with police.

Everett Lee was also among those Carter texted following the incident.

Lee was arrested but was not charged in connection with the case.

The messages were exchanged after the alleged gang rape, and Carter’s defense attorney sought to prevent them from being introduced as evidence at trial.

In a court filing submitted in September, his attorney contended that admitting the text messages as trial evidence would infringe on his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination.

Judge Gail Horne Ray has yet to issue a ruling.

The court document doesn’t differentiate who each text message was sent to.

Carter has pleaded not guilty to charges of first- and third-degree rape, with his trial scheduled to begin Dec. 7.

Both Carter and Washington maintain that their sexual encounters with Brooks were consensual.

Prosecutors allege that Carver drove the vehicle where Brooks was allegedly raped and recorded the encounter.

He has pleaded not guilty to charges of principal to rape and video voyeurism.

The men told police that Brooks asked to be taken home after the incident, providing multiple incorrect addresses before requesting to be let out near a subdivision, where they said she wandered into the street and was struck by a car.

The driver of the car that hit her remained on the scene and was ultimately cleared of charges.

“Maddie felt safe that night, she thought these were her friends and I think a lot of selfish choices were made that night, and ultimately it led to a horrific ending,” Brooks’ mother, Ashley Baustert, previously told Fox News Digital.

Fox News Digital has reached out to attorneys for all men.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

At least four concertgoers were injured during a dangerous crowd surge that left fans crushed against one another at a sold-out OsamaSon show inside Manhattan’s Terminal 5 on Thursday night.

The 23-year-old rapper was performing a show for Nike’s Jordan Brand when DJ Nino Andretti urged fans to rush to the merchandise booth for an exclusive giveaway near the end of the concert, around 10:30 p.m., at the Hell’s Kitchen venue, according to music publication The Fader.

Two revelers were taken to local hospitals in stable condition while two others refused medical care, the NYPD told The Post.

“Upon arrival, officers observed a disorderly crowd exiting the venue following a concert,” an NYPD spokesperson said. “Four individuals sustained minor injuries.”

“EMS transported two individuals to local hospitals in stable condition, while the remaining two refused medical attention on scene,” they added.

No arrests have been made.

Opened in 2007, the 3,000-capacity Terminal 5 is known for its intimate layout and tightly packed crowds during sold-out shows.

Video circulating online shows Andretti telling the crowd, “Y’all gotta rush to the merch booth, there’s an exclusive gift!” before concertgoers surged toward the merchandise area.

Fans were then seen piling on top of one another, screaming for help and struggling to escape, while injured concertgoers were carried out on stretchers to ambulances outside, according to footage.

“Almost died tn @ osamason in nyc.. i know i be over exaggerating and s–t, but being crushed under 2 people and seeing the guy under me completely unconscious mightve actually traumatized me,” one concertgoer posted to X.

Another attendee claimed multiple fans “passed out and people left with broken/dislocated bones.”

“This whole thing could’ve been avoided if he just went to the paramount like did the last time he toured in New York but he chose a notoriously bad venue instead and got his fans hurt in the process,” the attendee added, referencing the Brooklyn Paramount.

Even before the incident, fans were passing out due to the packed crowd during the opening DJ set, according to the Fader.

By the time OsamaSon took the stage around 9:15 p.m., fans near the front had little room to move.

“Every song — there were no breaks, no water, no breaks in the set, just onto the next song, just keep it going, keep it going, keep it going,” attendee Logan Lacy said.

“And it eventually got a lot tamer towards the end because people were just like, you know, it was just suffocating,” he added.

Thursday’s incident has renewed concerns about safety at Terminal 5, a venue that has faced criticism over packed shows, narrow hallways and bottlenecks that can make it difficult for crowds to move safely.

Ohio-born OsamaSon, whose real name is Amari Middleton, broke through with his 2023 debut mixtape “Osama Season” and has since built a following in the underground rap scene.

OsamaSon’s partnership with Nike’s Jordan Brand was announced last week alongside a campaign featuring the rapper and NFL star Jahmyr Gibbs wearing the Air Jordan 4 “Bred.”

Rapper Travis Scott, a Jordan Brand partner since 2017, was also at the center of a crowd surge at his 2021 Astroworld Festival in Houston, where 10 people were killed.

news.originalContent:
Pressure from within Sudan may achieve what international diplomacy has not.

It has been more than three years since war erupted in Sudan, and its consequences continue to worsen. More people continue to be displaced and require basic humanitarian assistance to survive. On the surface, the conflict appears set to continue indefinitely.

At a recent Security Council briefing, a United Nations official noted: “The picture is bleak. … The parties continue to show no credible commitment to compromise or to pursuing a negotiated pause in fighting. They are not moving closer to dialogue.”

This assessment reflects the international consensus so much so that the United States has chosen in recent months to heap sanction upon sanction in a bid to “raise the costs of continued conflict” for the warring sides and force them into ceasefire talks. But what the view from New York and Washington misses and what became obvious after only a few days in Khartoum this month is that the conditions for a ceasefire are rapidly emerging from within the country.

A perfect storm of financial collapse, military advances and humanitarian catastrophe, along with growing civilian demands, is creating the long-elusive pressure for a ceasefire that could well take hold before the fourth anniversary of the war next April.

Khartoum, Sudan’s beleaguered capital, is no longer the ghost town that it was throughout much of the war. International flights now arrive regularly at the city’s modest airport from Cairo, Riyadh and Doha, carrying Sudanese looking to restart the lives the war put on hold and businessmen sensing a ceasefire on the horizon and angling to get in on the ground floor of the country’s rebirth. At one of the city’s leading business hotels, the lobby was buzzing with British, Swiss and Saudi business groups there to close deals on everything from mining to commodity trading to reconstruction.

But Sudan’s leaders don’t just see the opportunities; they are also feeling the pressure of an economy in freefall. The week I was there, the Sudanese pound fell to a then-record low of 9,000 to the US dollar, compared with a pre-war average of 600. (The exchange rate now exceeds 10,000.) Petrol queues stretched for blocks, even for those lucky enough to be able to afford to fill their tanks. Many of Khartoum’s returnees, more than 2 million of the roughly 3.8 million people who fled, are struggling to buy groceries and keep the lights on. Worse still, farmers can no longer afford fertiliser, leaving much of the country’s most productive cropland lying fallow.

A senior official acknowledged to me privately that the war economy, which enabled Sudan’s army to procure the weapons needed to turn the tide of the war, is now the greatest source of pain for the country’s population. The pressure on Sudan’s leaders to reverse the economic decline is real and is creating a new demand to end the fighting.

Friendly states like Turkiye and Saudi Arabia have pitched in, pursuing agreements to secure fuel supplies and rebuild energy infrastructure, but such support remains limited and temporary. Protests over transit costs recently broke out in Atbara, the northern city where protests against skyrocketing bread prices began in December 2018, helping to spark Sudan’s 2019 democratic revolution. Economic protests unified the country before and could do so again, and the military knows it.

Beyond the economy, it is the military’s battlefield gains that are creating the conditions for it to contemplate a ceasefire. Army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan has promised to reclaim “every inch” of territory. He has succeeded in pushing back a new offensive in southeastern Sudan’s Blue Nile State and is advancing farther west in West Kordofan, where the army and its allied Joint Forces recently retook the strategic town of el-Khuwei and several surrounding areas, increasing the army’s control to roughly two-thirds of the country.

Fighting for control of the western region of Darfur, the only region almost entirely under the control of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary, could be costly and time-consuming. But a year after the fall of el-Fasher, the capital of North Darfur State, to the RSF amid atrocities that a UN fact-finding mission said bore the hallmarks of genocide, efforts to retake the area would demonstrate that the military’s commitment to unify the country wasn’t just battlefield bravado. Making inroads in Darfur would also paint the RSF into a corner and give the army both tactical gains and a strategic advantage in ceasefire discussions.

The final reason why a ceasefire has become so urgent is the spiralling humanitarian crisis in the country, which has been at crisis levels for months but could well become catastrophic by year’s end. Adding to the internal displacement, restrictions on humanitarian access and lost food production is this year’s “Super El Nino”, which has disrupted Sudan’s annual rains and devastated whatever meagre harvest was expected.

With more than 40 percent of the population already facing “acute food insecurity”, according to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification hunger monitor, projections suggested that Sudan’s hunger crisis could deteriorate dramatically by mid-2027 when food shortages are expected to be at their most severe. The only way to avoid or even mitigate that outcome would be through a ceasefire in the coming months that enables a massive influx of lifesaving aid.

As conditions on the ground make a ceasefire more urgent, Sudan’s own plans for the day after the fighting are becoming clearer. With each ceasefire proposal the military rejects, public demand for a deal grows as people become increasingly exhausted by the war.

Talk of an inter-Sudanese dialogue, political reconciliation and eventually elections is also becoming more common, creating greater expectations that fighting should soon come to an end and responsibility for day-to-day governance and service delivery be transferred to civilians. While these efforts remain inchoate, the demand for them is building.

Ultimately, it is the attitudes inside Sudan that will create the momentum for peace, not the external pressures and punitive measures employed by the international community. As conditions for civilians inside the country continue to deteriorate and the military’s position stabilises, there is hope on the horizon that a ceasefire could be achieved. The international community should focus on supporting these internal conditions before the dire warnings about the economy and humanitarian situation become reality.

A version of this article first appeared on Al Jazeera Arabic.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

He has succeeded in pushing back a new offensive in southeastern Sudan’s Blue Nile State and is advancing farther west in West Kordofan, where the army and its allied Joint Forces recently retook the strategic town of el-Khuwei and several surrounding areas, increasing the army’s control to roughly two-thirds of the country.

Fighting for control of the western region of Darfur, the only region almost entirely under the control of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary, could be costly and time-consuming. But a year after the fall of el-Fasher, the capital of North Darfur State, to the RSF amid atrocities that a UN fact-finding mission said bore the hallmarks of genocide, efforts to retake the area would demonstrate that the military’s commitment to unify the country wasn’t just battlefield bravado. Making inroads in Darfur would also paint the RSF into a corner and give the army both tactical gains and a strategic advantage in ceasefire discussions.

The final reason why a ceasefire has become so urgent is the spiralling humanitarian crisis in the country, which has been at crisis levels for months but could well become catastrophic by year’s end. Adding to the internal displacement, restrictions on humanitarian access and lost food production is this year’s “Super El Nino”, which has disrupted Sudan’s annual rains and devastated whatever meagre harvest was expected.

With more than 40 percent of the population already facing “acute food insecurity”, according to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification hunger monitor, projections suggested that Sudan’s hunger crisis could deteriorate dramatically by mid-2027 when food shortages are expected to be at their most severe. The only way to avoid or even mitigate that outcome would be through a ceasefire in the coming months that enables a massive influx of lifesaving aid.

As conditions on the ground make a ceasefire more urgent, Sudan’s own plans for the day after the fighting are becoming clearer. With each ceasefire proposal the military rejects, public demand for a deal grows as people become increasingly exhausted by the war.

Talk of an inter-Sudanese dialogue, political reconciliation and eventually elections is also becoming more common, creating greater expectations that fighting should soon come to an end and responsibility for day-to-day governance and service delivery be transferred to civilians. While these efforts remain inchoate, the demand for them is building.

Ultimately, it is the attitudes inside Sudan that will create the momentum for peace, not the external pressures and punitive measures employed by the international community. As conditions for civilians inside the country continue to deteriorate and the military’s position stabilises, there is hope on the horizon that a ceasefire could be achieved. The international community should focus on supporting these internal conditions before the dire warnings about the economy and humanitarian situation become reality.

news.originalContent:

Brooklyn’s Moritz Wagner had been in the NBA for nine years, alive for 20 more, and never played against his brother Franz in a game that counted.

This first one stung, having to watch his younger brother torch his team for 35 points, including a game-winner with 2.8 seconds left in a game the Nets had to have.

“I don’t care about him. I wanted to win the game. It’s one of the more conflicting games I’ve ever been a part of,” Moritz, who scored three points in 22 minutes, said afterward. “That is weird, but we’ve got enough problems going on. I can’t worry about nothing on the other side. I’m trying to win the game, and that one hurts.”

The Nets had already dropped three straight, including Wednesday’s humiliation against Chicago that prompted a team meeting.

Brooklyn jumped to a quick 17-11 lead against Orlando, then coughed up a 27-8 run.

The younger Wagner tore up Brooklyn’s defense, including 14 points in the third quarter alone. But it was his 15-footer that won it with 2.8 seconds remaining.

“He’s a great player. He’s gonna be an All-Star many times in this career. And great players make great plays,” Moritz said. “I don’t think we lost the game on that play. There are plenty of opportunities. We turned it over twice down the stretch. We took some questionable shots, didn’t make enough plays, and that’s what happens. Great player, make great plays.”

Moritz played for Michigan and was a 2018 first-round pick by Orlando, where he’d spent his entire career until inking with the Nets this summer.

Franz, four years his junior, had followed in his footsteps and starred for the Wolverines before being picked eighth overall by the Magic in 2021. He even lived with Moe until the latter came to Brooklyn in the summer.

“To be honest, it was one of the toughest things I’ve ever had to feel on a court. Too much going on, I was very anxious first half, clearly (not) focused on the game. I didn’t expect it would be this difficult,” said Moritz. “I’m glad we got this one out the way. I’m not sure how I’m gonna deal with that; to be determined. But we did it, and now it’s not a big deal anymore.”

Franz said: “My whole NBA career I played with him. The first time in my life playing against him. But as weird as it (was) … it’s a blessing to share the court with your family. Not a lot of people get to do that so that’s how I look at it.”

Starting point guard Nolan Traore left with a right hamstring injury in the third quarter and didn’t return.

Mikel Brown Jr. had a career-high-tying 18 points, including a dozen in that third period.

Danny Wolf started and had 20 points, the third-most in his career. Egor Dëmin came off the bench for the first time since November of his rookie season.

Paolo Banchero (right ankle) was out for Orlando.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

An Alabama man who claimed self-defense for shooting TikTok star Ophelia Nichols’ teenage son during a drug deal was acquitted of murder on Friday— as the influencer said that “justice had been stripped” from her family.

Reuben Gulley, 25, was found not guilty of killing 18-year-old Randon Lee after a jury deliberated for about an hour and a half before returning with the verdict that shocked Lee’s family and friends, according to WALA.

Nichols, known as “Mama Tot” and with over 12 million followers on TikTok, revealed that her husband burst into tears when the jury foreman shared the verdict in the packed courtroom.

“I have watched my husband break down sitting in that courtroom today while I did my best to hold it together for myself, for him, my children, our entire family,” Nichols wrote on Facebook.

“As I could feel the excited energy from the other side because their son was coming home, I slowly melted into my seat. Knowing that Justice had been stripped from my son and us, I couldn’t even describe what it did to my soul,” she wrote.

Gulley shot Lee inside his car when the teen attempted to sell him weed during an arranged drug deal outside a gas station in Prichard, Ala., on June 24, 2022.

Gulley had admitted during his trial on Thursday that he shot Lee during the drug meet-up in self-defense after the teen pulled a gun on him first.

Prosecutors had argued Gulley shot Lee to avoid paying $300 for the 2 ounces of weed the two had agreed on.

Security footage from the Pride gas station in Prichard, Ala., north of Mobile, captured a hooded Gulley stepping out of the passenger side of a car and going around to Lee’s car parked behind a gas pump.

Gulley testified that he got into the back seat of Lee’s car and pulled out 15 $20 bills to pay for the drugs before Lee allegedly pulled out a gun, leading to the deadly shooting.

The footage, played as evidence during the trial, didn’t show the moment of the shooting but did capture Gulley running back to the car with a gun in his hand as Lee drove off.

Gulley’s lawyer said there was a lack of evidence and a poor investigation by the Prichard Police Department to find his client guilty.

Attorney Chase Dearman accused detectives of not following up on leads or answering questions on how the alleged single gunshot from Gulley could result in a bullet remaining lodged in Lee’s body while also blasting a bullet hole through the windshield of the car.

“Of course, I’m satisfied, but more than anything else, I am relieved,” Dearman told WALA after the hearing. “I laid awake all night thinking certainly a Mobile County jury could not find somebody guilty on this kind of evidence, and I’m very, very happy.”

Morning Report delivers the latest news, videos, photos and more.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Prosecutors blamed the police department’s evidence collection and investigation process for acquittal.

“We believed in this case despite the problems with the investigation, because we had independent corroborating evidence,” Mobile County Chief Assistant District Attorney Jennifer Susman said.

“But there’s no denying that all of the issues with the Prichard Police Department have created a distraction to the jurors, and I believe that defense attorneys are trying to take full advantage of that. I’m very hopeful that as we continue to fight for justice, people will be able to focus on the veracity of the other evidence, and ultimately the right outcomes will be a result.”

Nichols blasted the verdict for Gulley as a punch to her family, as they were left with questions for the jury.

“We don’t know what, why or how the jurors came to that decision and I’m sure we will question that moment the rest of our lives,” Nichols wrote. “No remorse for our family. Zero regards for Randon’s life. What was done to our family was downright cruel and knowing that we are not alone in these situations is scary.

“I watched my daughter cry her eyes out today, I’ve only seen my husband cry like three times in the 20 years we’ve been married and he couldn’t control himself today,” she said through tears. “He lost it.”

news.originalContent:
His attacks on Arab lawmakers echo the incitement that preceded Rabin’s assassination and risk unleashing new violence.

Senior Consulting Fellow at the MENA Programme, Chatham House.

Politics is not for the faint-hearted, and debate and disagreement are integral to it. A number of politicians believe that the end justifies the means, but most know when they are approaching the red lines and when to stop.

Not Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s current prime minister. His repulsive response to the success of the Arab parties in last month’s general election unleashed his darkest racist demons.

Some might argue that this is simply another cynical tactic in his efforts to derail his political rivals’ attempts to form a government. Whether this is who he really is or simply a cynical politician at his core, governing through division makes little difference.

He is the prime minister, and his words and behaviour matter. When he legitimises and normalises this kind of language, he releases the racist genie from the bottle. Certain segments of his supporters may interpret it as a licence to resort to actual violence, and history has precedent for it.

Accusing all 19 elected members of the Knesset (MKs) representing predominantly Palestinian citizens of Israel, individually and collectively, of being supporters of terrorism and terrorists, while portraying those members of the Jewish/Zionist parties prepared to form a coalition with them as, for all intents and purposes, collaborators with those who support terrorism against Jews and seek the destruction of the “Jewish state”, amounts to declaring open season on them. In doing so, Netanyahu is abusing the protection afforded to him by his parliamentary immunity, making allegations for which there is not a shred of truth.

If anyone should know better, learn from his past mistakes and express profound remorse for such behaviour, it is Benjamin Netanyahu. No one is more closely associated with the atmosphere of incitement that preceded the assassination of Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin on November 4, 1995 than Netanyahu.

Rabin became the principal target of the Israeli right’s hatred after signing the Oslo Accords – in other words, for demonstrating the courage to pursue a peaceful end to the conflict between Israelis and Palestinians. The religious-messianic right, including several rabbis, issued a ruling known as din rodef (the law of the pursuer) against Rabin, accusing him of “ceding parts of the Land of Israel to Gentiles”. Yigal Amir, Rabin’s eventual assassin, cited this ruling as justification for his heinous crime. Amir pulled the trigger, but those who orchestrated and fed the campaign of hatred against Rabin bear considerable responsibility too, at the very least morally.

Netanyahu, who was chairman of the Likud party and leader of the opposition at the time, not only failed to condemn this behaviour but notoriously participated in a protest in Jerusalem during which Rabin’s image was portrayed in a Nazi uniform. Rabin’s widow, Leah, later recalled: “There was a Likud rally in Jerusalem not too long ago. They put the figure of Yitzhak, my husband, in the uniform of a Nazi leader and Mr Netanyahu was there. He later talked against it, but he was there, and he didn’t stop it.”

She never forgave him for that. He never apologised or expressed regret.

Several months later, Netanyahu was elected prime minister. Perhaps, in his mind, this electoral victory exonerated him from any responsibility for creating the atmosphere that led to Rabin’s assassination. It may also have reinforced his belief that divisive politics pays off and can take him where he has always felt he belongs: The prime minister’s office.

Now, caught between a sense of entitlement to remain in power that appears stronger than ever and the fear that relinquishing office could jeopardise his efforts to prevent his corruption trial from reaching its conclusion, Netanyahu is allowing racial hatred to pour out of him unabated.

It began during the election campaign, when he foresaw that his chances of forming the next government were slim. It escalated dramatically on election day, when he once again resorted to his vile dog-whistle tactics in a last-ditch attempt to mobilise his supporters. He warned of surging Arab voter turnout and, by that, at least implicitly questioned the legitimacy of their votes compared with the Jewish ones, as they couldn’t bear their success. But that was only the beginning. The day after the election, Netanyahu and his ultra-right-wing partners turned up the volume, raising allegations of irregularities in Arab communities to advance a narrative of a “stolen” election.

Worse was to come. What should have been days of celebrating Israeli democracy, the swearing-in of the new Knesset, became another opportunity for Netanyahu to abuse his parliamentary privilege. Instead of delivering a speech that might have helped unite the nation after a bruising election campaign, he embarked on a jingoistic horror show.

He accused Gadi Eisenkot, whom President Isaac Herzog had tasked with forming a government because he enjoyed the support of a majority of MKs, and his political partners of seeking to establish a government dependent on parties that, according to Netanyahu, “agree that the Jewish state must be destroyed”. He went on to claim that these parties differed only over the kind of Palestinian state they wanted to see emerge from the ruins of the Jewish state: “Whether an Islamic state in the Muslim Brotherhood mould, like Hamas in Gaza, or a nationalist Palestinian state in the Fatah mould. That is the whole difference.”

This amounts to nothing less than portraying Arab political representatives as a fifth column or traitors, while depicting those prepared to form a government with them as collaborators with this supposed ambition, or as dangerously naive for failing to recognise it.

When Netanyahu and his political partners insist that their accusations are not directed at the Arab population, even though Arab citizens had voted in record numbers for these very parties only days earlier, they are either playing innocent or insulting the intelligence of both Arab citizens and the wider public.

Not so long ago, Netanyahu himself offered Mansour Abbas and his Ra’am party the opportunity to join his own government when it suited his political interests. Yet when his rivals contemplate doing precisely the same thing, he shamelessly incites against them.

Let us not forget that Netanyahu is the politician who legitimised the messianic far right and normalised sharing power with its representatives in government. He appointed Itamar Ben-Gvir, who had been convicted of incitement to racism and supporting a terrorist organisation, as minister of national security. This is the same Ben-Gvir who first gained notoriety by stealing the emblem from the car of then-Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin, displaying it on television and declaring: “We got to his car, and we’ll get to him too.” Netanyahu is opportunistic and cynical to the very end, but by now the distinction between him and the Kahanist Ben-Gvir has become paper-thin.

The warning signs are there, written on the wall in capital letters. The incitement of 1995 helped create the atmosphere that led to Rabin’s assassination. The scale and intensity of today’s incitement could once again lead an extremist zealot to pull the trigger, this time against an Arab or Jewish politician seeking to work with Arab political representatives. It could also encourage attacks against Arab citizens, potentially escalating into widespread communal violence or even civil war, as extremists convince themselves that they are acting in accordance with their leader’s wishes to prevent the supposed destruction of the Jewish state.

Israel is on the brink of political violence. And Benjamin Netanyahu bears a very substantial share of the responsibility for bringing it there.

He appointed Itamar Ben-Gvir, who had been convicted of incitement to racism and supporting a terrorist organisation, as minister of national security. This is the same Ben-Gvir who first gained notoriety by stealing the emblem from the car of then-Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin, displaying it on television and declaring: “We got to his car, and we’ll get to him too.” Netanyahu is opportunistic and cynical to the very end, but by now the distinction between him and the Kahanist Ben-Gvir has become paper-thin.

The warning signs are there, written on the wall in capital letters. The incitement of 1995 helped create the atmosphere that led to Rabin’s assassination. The scale and intensity of today’s incitement could once again lead an extremist zealot to pull the trigger, this time against an Arab or Jewish politician seeking to work with Arab political representatives. It could also encourage attacks against Arab citizens, potentially escalating into widespread communal violence or even civil war, as extremists convince themselves that they are acting in accordance with their leader’s wishes to prevent the supposed destruction of the Jewish state.

Israel is on the brink of political violence. And Benjamin Netanyahu bears a very substantial share of the responsibility for bringing it there.

The wife and two young children senselessly killed in a chilling New Mexico murder-suicide “were so loved and will be so missed” — as gut-wrenching photos of the trio were revealed.

Alayna Reyes, 28, was gunned down by her husband Marcus Reyes Sr., who also shot and killed the couple’s son, Marcus Jr., 8, and daughter, Anastacia, 6, inside their East Mesa home on Thursday morning, according to Las Cruces Police.

Reyes Sr., 28, then fatally shot himself, cops said.

An online fundraiser launched by Alayna Reyes’ family Friday mourned the shocking tragedy: “This unimaginable loss has left us heartbroken.”

“They were so loved and will be missed,” her aunt, Kim Vallejos, wrote on the GoFundMe, which had raised more than $14,000 as of early Saturday morning.

“As we navigate this difficult time, we are also faced with the unexpected financial burden of arranging their funerals and giving them the loving farewell they deserve,” Vallejos added.

Heartbreaking photos of Alayna Reyes and her two kids were shared alongside the fundraiser — one of which showed Marcus Jr. and Anastacia wrapping themselves around their mom with an affectionate hug.

In separate pictures with each child, the beaming-with-pride mom Alayna is snapped next to Marcus Jr. in a park and Anastacia at the beach, while in another, the kids are grinning ear to ear as they enjoy ice cream.

Their bodies – along with Marcus Reyes Sr.’s – were discovered by authorities around 10 a.m. Thursday after a female relative failed to get in touch with the family and called police to conduct a welfare check.

The suburban community, “a very calm, quiet area,” according to neighbor Erika Sorensen, was rocked by news of the horror on Lunetta Court.

“It’s very unnerving that it’s just right there,” Sorensen told ABC-7.

“Nothing like this has ever happened. It’s heartbreaking. It’s so sad,” said another neighbor Katie Albright.

Albright, who has lived in the neighborhood since 2017, said “everybody’s talking about how we’re processing it with our kids, and how we’re processing it with each other.”

“And, you know,” she said, “looking for ways that we can hopefully support the family.”

If you are struggling with suicidal thoughts, you can dial the 24/7 National Suicide Prevention Hotline at 988 or go to SuicidePreventionLifeline.org.

Eisenkot’s fragile alliance must overcome deep ideological divisions to turn its opposition into a government.

As negotiations over the formation of Israel’s next government approach their first deadline of December 6, caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appears to be seeking to exploit divisions within the opposition “change” alliance trying to oust him.

On Wednesday, he held an undeclared meeting with one of its leading figures, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, in a move that has prompted accusations that Netanyahu is attempting to fracture the bloc from within.

The meeting, which lasted two and a half hours, was described by Netanyahu’s office as a “security briefing”. Sources within the opposition alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot, however, characterised it as a “strategic disaster”, according to Israeli media.

Bennett had not informed Eisenkot of the meeting in advance, sources told the outlet Ynet. During a subsequent gathering of opposition leaders, Bennett is reported to have argued that they should try to pursue the possibility of a unity government with Netanyahu, Channel 12 reported.

Bennett, a right-winger, is among several prominent figures in the opposition alliance who have previously served in Netanyahu-led governments. Eisenkot himself joined Netanyahu’s emergency unity government following the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, serving as a minister without portfolio and a member of the war cabinet.

Avigdor Lieberman, meanwhile – another right-wing member of the opposition bloc – served as Netanyahu’s foreign minister and defence minister.

“Netanyahu is trying to break up the [opposition] bloc for change through Bennett,” a senior figure in the Eisenkot-led alliance told Ynet in an article referencing the numerous pledges by opposition leaders, including Bennett, never to serve within a Netanyahu-led coalition again.

However, given the broad array of ideologies among the coalition leaders, stretching from the hard-right policies of Lieberman to the relatively left-wing platform of Democrats’ leader Yair Golan, and many having previously worked with Netanyahu, it remains unclear how long the bloc can maintain its unity.

Bennett himself was once among Netanyahu’s closest political allies, serving in several of his governments before breaking with him in 2021, when the opportunity arose to form an alternative administration with centrist Yair Lapid. Bennett and Lapid subsequently assembled a cross-party coalition that ended Netanyahu’s 12 consecutive years in office, with Bennett taking the premiership for the first half of its term. But he still shares many policy positions with Netanyahu.

So how cohesive is the opposition coalition, and what could be its potential breaking points?

All of the bloc’s members supported Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza – at least at its start – as well as its attacks on several regional states, including Iran and Lebanon.

In terms of domestic policy, however, there are marked differences between members of the alliance.

Both the bloc’s leader, former Israeli military Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, and Bennett’s electoral partner, Yair Lapid, are regarded as relatively centrist figures. By contrast, Bennett and Lieberman are firmly on the right, divided largely by their attitudes towards religion: Bennett is a religious nationalist, while Liberman is a staunchly secular politician with a background in Israel’s Russian-speaking community, increasingly at odds with Israel’s powerful religious political currents.

Standing apart is the left-wing Yair Golan, a supporter of a two-state solution with the Palestinians and an outspoken critic of settler pogroms in the occupied West Bank, which he has accused the government of encouraging or tolerating.

Beyond the prospect of Netanyahu – Israel’s longest-serving prime minister – continually attempting to undermine them, Eisenkot faces the formidable task of finding the additional 13 seats needed for a parliamentary majority. His bloc holds just 48 of the parliament’s 120 seats after the October 27 elections, leaving him dependent on bridging deep political divides among his allies if he is to form a government capable of governing.

Golan has already met political leaders from parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel and spoken enthusiastically about forming a government with their support. However, that suggestion has been rejected by the rest of the bloc, and has provoked fierce opposition, with right-wing protesters even threatening civil war at the prospect.

Lieberman, whose Yisrael Beytenu party holds seven seats, has been particularly emphatic in rejecting any government dependent on Palestinian support. However, his longstanding and highly vocal opposition to the de facto exemption of ultra-Orthodox Jewish men from military service appears to be softening in the face of another possibility: the 13 seats held by the ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism.

Lieberman’s willingness to compromise on conscription risks undermining one of his central electoral promises, as well as those of other opposition leaders, and could prompt a backlash from supporters.

In August, Bennett dismissed Eisenkot’s proposal to allow limited exemptions from military conscription that would cover the ultra-Orthodox as an “insane mistake”, warning that ultra-Orthodox politicians Aryeh Deri and Moshe Gafni would “run circles around” him. Eisenkot subsequently countered, accusing Bennett and Lieberman of engaging in “old politics” and damaging the opposition’s electoral prospects by refusing to agree that the largest party in the alliance should lead the next government.

Lieberman, just weeks before the election, branded Eisenkot “Gantz 2.0” –  referring to former defence minister Benny Gantz, who joined Netanyahu’s government in 2020 despite campaigning against him – accusing Eisenkot of secretly pursuing a deal with Netanyahu and acting out of personal ambition. Golan, meanwhile, told Lieberman several days after the election that, if he was to continue to insist on a government that avoids conscripting ultra-Orthodox men, he was “welcome to form one with Netanyahu”.

Their previous assessments of Netanyahu have not always been so harsh.

In 2020, Bennett told reporters that, despite their personal differences, he respected Netanyahu “very much”, adding that Israel had “won a victory” by having him in office for so long and that he had “done great things” for the country.

Lieberman, meanwhile, told The Jerusalem Post in 2019 that he wished Netanyahu “only really good results” and hoped that he would be acquitted on the corruption charges that he has since cited, on numerous occasions, as evidence that the prime minister is unfit for office.

The Lakers continue to look like a team in need of the benefits that are supposed to come from this stretch in Southern California.

Because after looking like one of the NBA’s best teams for 3 ½ weeks regardless of the competition, they’ve struggled against some of the league’s bottom-feeders during their four-game homestand.

That was once again the case on Friday night, with the Lakers barely beating the lowly one-win Kings, 106-104, at Crypto.com Arena to get back on track after losing to the Jazz on Wednesday.

After Walker Kessler missed a pair of free throws with the Lakers up by two points with five seconds left in the fourth, Zach LaVine grabbed the defensive rebound and dribbled up the court before firing a 29-footer that hit the front rim to secure the victory for the Lakers.

But until the final buzzer sounded, there was an unease about whether the Lakers were going to lose back-to-back games for the first time.

They trailed 62-54 at halftime, with a general malaise from Tuesday’s overtime win over the Hornets and Wednesday’s loss to the Jazz carrying over into Friday.

It showed defensively, with the Lakers allowing too many drives to the rim.

It showed with the seven first-quarter turnovers they committed, which directly led to 11 Kings points.

But the Lakers, led by Luka Dončić (25 points, eight assists, four rebounds and two steals), found enough of the groove they had been searching for in the second half to turn what was an 11-point deficit in the third into an eight-point lead in the fourth.

And they held on just long enough to ensure they entered the weekend with a 14-3 record before a two-day break before hosting the Jazz again on Monday.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Major League Baseball players rejected management’s proposal for an international amateur draft, instead asking Friday for larger signing bonus pools under the current system and more rewards for small-market teams in another sign the sport is heading to a lockout next month.

Management has tried unsuccessfully for more than two decades to get an international draft and in June proposed it start with 12 rounds in 2027.

“We are committed to negotiating a system that preserves opportunities for future generations of players, protects young prospects from exploitation, and provides flexibility without further burdening international players with new artificial restrictions like a draft,” players’ association head Bruce Meyer said in a statement after a bargaining session in New York.

MLB’s five-year collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. EST on Dec. 1 and management is expected to immediately lock out players in the sport’s 10th work stoppage since 1972. Owners are pushing for a salary cap, which players say they never will agree to, sparking a confrontation that threatens the 2027 season.

An amateur draft was established for residents of the U.S. and Canada in 1965 and extended to residents of U.S. territories such as Puerto Rico in 1990. A signing bonus pool system started in 2012 restrained team spending for amateurs residing outside those areas, primarily teenagers from the Dominican Republic, Venezuela, Colombia, Mexico and Panama. Players outside the U.S. are eligible to sign as young as 16, and it’s common for players, their families and trainers to strike handshake deals with teams at 13 or 14 in a system rife with corruption.

“We continue to believe it is long past time to reform the system in ways that would address longstanding challenges and benefit future players,” MLB spokesperson Glen Caplin said. “The enhanced transparency of the international draft that we have proposed best addresses the root causes of corruption in the current system.”

Caplin also said MLB dropped its proposal that would have made high school players ineligible for the domestic amateur draft, citing “feedback we received from the MLBPA.”

The union proposed teams entering into any agreements with international amateurs ahead of a signing period lose the right to sign the involved player, forfeit pool space in the amount of the agreed-upon signing bonus and their entire pool space in the subsequent signing period. The lost pool space would be redistributed to other clubs and a violation would result in a minimum $200,000 fine. In addition, the sides would hire a joint compliance officer.

MLB has tried to gain an international draft since 2001 only to be repeatedly rebuffed by players.

In its latest proposal, management included $200 million in signing bonus pools for 2027, roughly equal to 2026 international amateur spending, and said it would retain an unlimited amount of passed over players signing for up to $10,000 each. Management proposed hard slots for each draft pick and asked the minimum signing age for international amateurs to be raised to 18 from 17 on the Sept. 1 of their signing year.

Players proposed increases in the three basic team pool levels in 2027: from $8,034,900 to $8.5 million, from $7,357,100 to $7.75 million and from $6,679,200 to $7 million. The figures would grow in future years at the same rate as industry revenue.

Teams would be allowed to exceed their bonus pools but would be taxed on their overage and if 15% or more over could lose future pool amounts. Additional pool space of up to $2 million would be added to club rewards in the Prospect Promotion Incentive begun under the current CBA.

The union asked that the limit of bonuses not counting against the pools be raised to $75,000 through 2029 and then $100,000, and that the limit of 60% additional pool allotment a team can acquire be dropped along with the requirement traded allotments be in $250,000 increments. Players signing below $75,000 would be eligible for $25,000 promotion bonuses if assigned to a complex team or a player development league club, money to be funded centrally by MLB.

In addition, the union proposed that teams receiving revenue sharing money be able to increase their pool by $1 million in a single signing period over a five-year agreement and by $500,000 in each period following a postseason appearance. Those teams also would be able to sign two draft-eligible players to a major league contract from 2027-31 but would lose $4 million per player in allotment.

Players asked to set up separate signing bonus pools for eligible players with limited foreign professional experience, preventing future players in that situation from competing for signing bonus pool money with teenage prospects — as Roki Sasaki did when he signed with the Los Angeles Dodgers before the 2025 season.

“Our proposals help build upon baseball’s advances as an international game, while safeguarding the interests of young athletes who are the future of our sport,” Meyer said.

MLB’s five-year collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. EST on Dec. 1 and management is expected to immediately lock out players in the sport’s 10th work stoppage since 1972. Owners are pushing for a salary cap, which players say they never will agree to, sparking a confrontation that threatens the 2027 season.

An amateur draft was established for residents of the U.S. and Canada in 1965 and extended to residents of U.S. territories such as Puerto Rico in 1990. A signing bonus pool system started in 2012 restrained team spending for amateurs residing outside those areas, primarily teenagers from the Dominican Republic, Venezuela, Colombia, Mexico and Panama. Players outside the U.S. are eligible to sign as young as 16, and it’s common for players, their families and trainers to strike handshake deals with teams at 13 or 14 in a system rife with corruption.

“We continue to believe it is long past time to reform the system in ways that would address longstanding challenges and benefit future players,” MLB spokesperson Glen Caplin said. “The enhanced transparency of the international draft that we have proposed best addresses the root causes of corruption in the current system.”

Caplin also said MLB dropped its proposal that would have made high school players ineligible for the domestic amateur draft, citing “feedback we received from the MLBPA.”

The union proposed teams entering into any agreements with international amateurs ahead of a signing period lose the right to sign the involved player, forfeit pool space in the amount of the agreed-upon signing bonus and their entire pool space in the subsequent signing period. The lost pool space would be redistributed to other clubs and a violation would result in a minimum $200,000 fine. In addition, the sides would hire a joint compliance officer.

MLB has tried to gain an international draft since 2001 only to be repeatedly rebuffed by players.

In its latest proposal, management included $200 million in signing bonus pools for 2027, roughly equal to 2026 international amateur spending, and said it would retain an unlimited amount of passed over players signing for up to $10,000 each. Management proposed hard slots for each draft pick and asked the minimum signing age for international amateurs to be raised to 18 from 17 on the Sept. 1 of their signing year.

Players proposed increases in the three basic team pool levels in 2027: from $8,034,900 to $8.5 million, from $7,357,100 to $7.75 million and from $6,679,200 to $7 million. The figures would grow in future years at the same rate as industry revenue.

Teams would be allowed to exceed their bonus pools but would be taxed on their overage and if 15% or more over could lose future pool amounts. Additional pool space of up to $2 million would be added to club rewards in the Prospect Promotion Incentive begun under the current CBA.

The union asked that the limit of bonuses not counting against the pools be raised to $75,000 through 2029 and then $100,000, and that the limit of 60% additional pool allotment a team can acquire be dropped along with the requirement traded allotments be in $250,000 increments. Players signing below $75,000 would be eligible for $25,000 promotion bonuses if assigned to a complex team or a player development league club, money to be funded centrally by MLB.

In addition, the union proposed that teams receiving revenue sharing money be able to increase their pool by $1 million in a single signing period over a five-year agreement and by $500,000 in each period following a postseason appearance. Those teams also would be able to sign two draft-eligible players to a major league contract from 2027-31 but would lose $4 million per player in allotment.

Players asked to set up separate signing bonus pools for eligible players with limited foreign professional experience, preventing future players in that situation from competing for signing bonus pool money with teenage prospects — as Roki Sasaki did when he signed with the Los Angeles Dodgers before the 2025 season.

“Our proposals help build upon baseball’s advances as an international game, while safeguarding the interests of young athletes who are the future of our sport,” Meyer said.

news.originalContent:
Saudi Arabia issues emergency alerts in Riyadh for the third night in a row, as the Houthis threaten ports and a power station.

The Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government said it has intercepted three ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Houthi rebels towards Riyadh, after a flurry of emergency alerts in the Saudi capital.

The attack early on Saturday morning came two days after a Houthi strike damaged the Public Investment Fund tower, the headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund and Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper.

It was the third day in a row that Saudi Arabia issued and quickly lifted alerts for Riyadh.

Hours later, the coalition said that it destroyed another drone fired by the Houthis towards the kingdom’s south. It did not say which province was targeted.

Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency had issued eight public emergency alerts during a 24-hour period starting at 7:30am Saudi time (04:30 GMT) on Friday.

In Yemen, the Saudi-led coalition said earlier on Friday that it carried out a “special operation” against the Houthi-held Red Sea port of Hodeidah, as well as “military targets” in the capital, Sanaa.

Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said the strikes hit “operational capabilities at Hodeidah port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles”, the AFP news agency reported.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government has defended the coalition strikes on Hodeidah port, accusing the Houthis of using its facilities to receive smuggled Iranian weapons and conduct military operations.

The Houthis responded by threatening to attack Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports, warning airlines that Saudi Arabia’s airspace was “unsafe”.

They also threatened Riyadh’s financial centre and a power station in Al-Shuqaiq, in the southwest.

The United Nations said it was following the escalation “with concern”.

It warned that continued fighting could threaten vital supply routes for humanitarian aid in Yemen.

news.originalContent:
Paris criminal court finds racism was an aggravating factor in the 2020 assault of Black music producer Michel Zecler.

A French court has sentenced three police officers to serve time for assaulting a Black music producer in 2020, acknowledging the racist motives of the beating in a rare ruling against police brutality.

In the judgement delivered on Friday, the Paris criminal court found the victim, Michel Zecler, 47, consistent in his account and deemed that racism was an aggravating factor in the assault.

An investigation into the incident showed that the officers pushed into the entrance of Zecler’s office and beat him.

The officers attacked Zecler outside his studio in Paris on November 21, 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, justifying the assault as being for his failure to wear a mandatory mask and allegedly grabbing one of their weapons.

Zecler’s security cameras recorded the attack, which left him with head trauma, a wound to the lip and scalp, and a complete rupture of his biceps tendon.

The court noted that Zecler told a Black police officer who was handcuffing him after the beating that he had been subjected to racial slurs. He repeated the allegation at the police station and again on the way to the hospital, and he also told his loved ones.

The court added that the officers’ falsification of the police report damaged their credibility when they denied using racist insults.

The court sentenced Aurelien Lapersonne, 29, to five years in jail, including three suspended. Philippe Tondeux, 50, was sentenced to five years, including three-and-a-half suspended. Pierre Plantier, 37, was sentenced to five years, four of which were suspended, and was to serve the one year with an ankle tag instead of behind bars.

A crowd applauded Zecler as he stepped out of the hearing, according to the AFP news agency.

“Justice has been done. It has restored a man’s dignity and allowed him to begin rebuilding himself,” his lawyer, Serge Money, said.

All three officers apologised to Zecler earlier on Friday, with Plantier in tears, AFP reported.

French victims and researchers say police violence is systemic, but guilty verdicts in alleged police brutality cases are rare in the country.

In 2024, a judge handed suspended prison sentences to three officers who caused permanent rectal injuries to a Black man, Theo Luhaka, during a stop-and-search in 2017.

Last year, a report by France’s rights chief found that young men “perceived as Arab, black or from North Africa” are four times more likely to be stopped than the rest of the population.

news.originalContent:
دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا، در نخستین نشست خبری خود پس از دیدار سه‌جانبه با رهبران چین و روسیه، گفت که روند قیمت بنزین در آمریکا تا حدی به چگونگی حل‌وفصل اختلافات با ایران بستگی دارد. او ضمن دفاع از تصمیم خود برای آغاز جنگ با ایران، دیدار با رهبران چین و روسیه را موفقیت‌آمیز توصیف کرد و از احتمال دستیابی به توافقی برای پایان جنگ اوکراین سخن گفت. آقای ترامپ همچنین تهدید کرد که شرکت‌های آمریکایی را از ساخت مراکز داده هوش مصنوعی در خارج از آن کشور منع خواهد کرد.

دونالد ترامپ روز جمعه ۲۹ آبان (۲۰ نوامبر) در نشستی خبری در کاخ سفید گفت که قیمت بنزین پیش از آغاز عملیات نظامی آمریکا علیه ایران پایین بود و پیش‌بینی کرد که به‌زودی قیمت سوخت به میزان قابل‌توجهی کاهش یابد.

او گفت: «به‌زودی شاهد قیمت‌های بسیار، بسیار پایین خواهید بود. قیمت بنزین پیش از اقدام نظامی محدود آمریکا علیه ایران پایین بود.»

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا افزود: «قیمت بنزین از اینجا به بعد تا حدی به این بستگی دارد که تکلیف‌مان را با ایران چطور روشن کنیم.»

آقای ترامپ بار دیگر تکرار کرد که ایران خواهان توافق با آمریکاست، اما حاضر نیست توافقی را بپذیرد که از نظر او قابل قبول باشد.

او گفت: «ما می‌خواهیم به یک توافق واقعی برسیم، نه یک توافق ساختگی.»

آقای ترامپ همچنین مقام‌های جمهوری اسلامی را متهم کرد که طی ۵۱ سال گذشته دیگران را فریب داده‌اند.

اشاره او به ۵۱ سال سابقه رفتار حکومت ایران در حالی است که جمهوری اسلامی در سال ۱۳۵۷، یعنی ۴۷ سال پیش، تاسیس شد. رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا پیش‌تر نیز از عدد ۵۱ سال استفاده کرده، اما توضیح نداده است که مبدأ این محاسبه را چه رویدادی در نظر می‌گیرد.

در سال ۱۹۷۵، چهار سال پیش از انقلاب ایران، دو افسر نیروی هوایی آمریکا به نام‌های پل شفر و جک ترنر که در هیئت مستشاری نظامی آمریکا در ایران خدمت می‌کردند، در تهران ترور شدند. اسناد وزارت خارجه آمریکا این ترورها را به اعضای سازمان مجاهدین خلق نسبت داده‌اند. سازمان مجاهدین خلق این اتهام را رد کرده است.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا در بخش دیگری از این نشست، گزارش‌ها درباره نارضایتی خود از اظهارات جی‌دی ونس، معاونش، پس از شکست جمهوری‌خواهان در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای کنگره را رد کرد.

آقای ونس جنگ با ایران را از عوامل شکست جمهوری‌خواهان در این انتخابات دانسته بود.

آقای ترامپ گفت: «اتفاقاً بیانیه خوبی بود. قطعاً جنگ بر قیمت سوخت اثر گذاشت، اما بسیار کمتر از آنچه تصور می‌شد.»

او با دفاع دوباره از تصمیم خود برای آغاز جنگ با ایران افزود که این جنگ اجتناب‌ناپذیر بود و اگر به گذشته بازگردد، بار دیگر همان تصمیم را خواهد گرفت.

آقای ترامپ گفت: «من فکر می‌کردم قیمت نفت به ۳۰۰ دلار برای هر بشکه برسد، اما الان تقریباً به ۸۰ دلار برای هر بشکه رسیده است.»

او همچنین مدعی شد که در هفته گذشته رکورد انتقال نفت از تنگه هرمز ثبت شده است.

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا با اشاره به محاصره دریایی ایران، از نیروی دریایی و ارتش این کشور تشکر کرد و گفت آمریکا «کنترل کامل» تنگه هرمز را در اختیار دارد.

جنگ ایران و اختلال در کشتیرانی از تنگه هرمز طی ماه‌های گذشته بر بازار جهانی انرژی و قیمت سوخت تأثیر گذاشته است. تنگه هرمز یکی از مهم‌ترین گذرگاه‌های انتقال نفت و گاز جهان است.

آقای ترامپ در بخش دیگری از نشست خبری با اشاره به سرکوب اعتراضات دی‌ماه ۱۴۰۴ در ایران، اتهام‌های تندی را متوجه مقام‌های جمهوری اسلامی کرد.

او گفت که حکومت ایران طی هشت ماه گذشته «۷۵ هزار معترض را کشته است.»

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا گفت: «من مقام‌های ایران را می‌شناسم و صادقانه بگویم، آنها دیوانه‌اند. حاکمان ایران گروهی بسیار شرور هستند.»

او همچنین با اشاره به دیدار اخیر خود با رهبران روسیه و چین گفت که در این نشست بر ضرورت جلوگیری از دستیابی ایران به سلاح هسته‌ای تأکید کرده است.

آقای ترامپ در ادامه، گزارش‌ها و انتقادها درباره کاهش ذخایر تسلیحاتی آمریکا بر اثر جنگ با ایران را رد کرد و جو بایدن، رئیس‌جمهور پیشین آمریکا، را مسئول کاهش ذخایر مهمات کشورش دانست.

او گفت که دولت بایدن با ارسال موشک و کمک‌های مالی گسترده به اوکراین، انبارهای تسلیحاتی آمریکا را خالی کرده است.

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا می‌گوید که دولت پیشین علاوه بر ارسال موشک، ۳۵۰ میلیارد دلار پول نقد نیز به اوکراین داده است، در حالی که دولت کنونی آمریکا در ازای تسلیحات ارسالی پول دریافت می‌کند.

آقای ترامپ همچنین از ساخت ۲۱ کارخانه تولید تجهیزات نظامی، از جمله سامانه‌های پاتریوت، موشک‌های تاماهاوک و سامانه‌های دفاع موشکی تاد، در سراسر آمریکا خبر داد و گفت که کشورش در حال تکمیل ذخایر تسلیحاتی خود است.

منبع تصویر، Win McNamee/Getty Images

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا در بخش دیگری از نشست خبری، دیدار سه‌جانبه روز پنجشنبه خود با شی جین‌پینگ، رئیس‌جمهور چین، و ولادیمیر پوتین، رئیس‌جمهور روسیه، در شهر شنژن چین را موفقیت‌آمیز توصیف کرد، اما جزئیاتی درباره پیشرفت احتمالی مذاکرات صلح ارائه نداد.

او انتقادها درباره اینکه این نشست ممکن است نشانه نزدیکی آمریکا به رقبای این کشور تلقی شود را رد کرد و گفت که برگزاری چنین دیداری نشان‌دهنده احترامی است که آمریکا در دوران ریاست‌جمهوری او از آن برخوردار است.

آقای ترامپ گفت که ولادیمیر پوتین تمایل خود را برای پایان دادن به جنگ اوکراین ابراز کرده است.

او افزود: «فکر می‌کنم احتمال بسیار خوبی وجود دارد که بتوانیم این کار را انجام دهیم.»

رهبران آمریکا، چین و روسیه پس از نشست سه‌جانبه خود بیانیه مشترکی درباره مسائل بین‌المللی منتشر کردند که از جمله بر جلوگیری از جنگ هسته‌ای و همکاری در زمینه تامین انرژی تأکید داشت.

با این حال، در این بیانیه به جنگ اوکراین یا جنگ ایران اشاره مشخصی نشده و این نشست به اعلام توافقی برای پایان هیچ‌یک از این دو جنگ منجر نشده است.

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا همچنین در ارزیابی سفر اخیر خود به آسیا گفت که در جریان این سفر دو توافق تجاری جدید به دست آورده و انتظار دارد حدود ۱۰ توافق دیگر نیز «خیلی زود» نهایی شود.

آقای ترامپ این توافق‌ها و دیدار با رهبران چین و روسیه را از دستاوردهای سفر خود توصیف کرد.

او در نشست خبری کاخ سفید تاکید کرد که آمریکا در روابط اقتصادی و سیاسی با دیگر کشورها از موضع قدرت مذاکره می‌کند.

منبع تصویر، Bloomberg via Getty Images

دونالد ترامپ در بخش دیگری از نشست خبری گفت که قصد دارد شرکت‌های آمریکایی را از ساخت مراکز داده هوش مصنوعی در خارج از ایالات متحده منع کند و شرکت‌هایی را که از این سیاست پیروی نکنند، با مالیات سنگین روبه‌رو سازد.

او گفت: «می‌خواهیم همه این فعالیت‌ها را در کشور خودمان نگه داریم.»

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا با اشاره به رقابت با چین در زمینه هوش مصنوعی افزود: «اجازه نمی‌دهیم شرکت‌های ما در خارج از کشور مراکز داده بسازند، چون چین همه آنها را تصاحب خواهد کرد و ما اجازه چنین اتفاقی را نمی‌دهیم.»

آقای ترامپ جزئیاتی درباره چگونگی اجرای این طرح ارائه نکرد و گفت که حتی اعضای دولتش نیز برای نخستین بار از این تصمیم مطلع می‌شوند.

شرکت‌های بزرگ فناوری آمریکا، از جمله گوگل و متا، در سال‌های اخیر سرمایه‌گذاری‌های گسترده‌ای برای ساخت مراکز داده در خارج از آن کشور انجام داده‌اند.

گوگل از جمله در ماه سپتامبر از برنامه سرمایه‌گذاری ۱۳ میلیارد یورویی در زیرساخت‌های هوش مصنوعی در فنلاند خبر داده بود.

مراکز داده نقش اساسی در توسعه هوش مصنوعی دارند و رایانه‌ها، پردازنده‌های پیشرفته و سرورهای مورد نیاز برای اجرای سامانه‌های هوش مصنوعی در این مراکز نگهداری می‌شوند.

سخنان آقای ترامپ در حالی مطرح می‌شود که دولت آمریکا اوایل هفته جاری محدودیت‌های تازه‌ای برای صادرات تراشه‌های پیشرفته رایانه‌ای اعلام کرد تا بر دسترسی شرکت‌های چینی به فناوری آمریکایی نظارت بیشتری داشته باشد.

هنوز مشخص نیست که پیشنهاد آقای ترامپ برای ممنوعیت ساخت مراکز داده در خارج از آمریکا چگونه و از چه زمانی اجرا خواهد شد.

دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا، در نخستین نشست خبری خود پس از دیدار سه‌جانبه با رهبران چین و روسیه، گفت که روند قیمت بنزین در آمریکا تا حدی به چگونگی حل‌وفصل اختلافات با ایران بستگی دارد. او ضمن دفاع از تصمیم خود برای آغاز جنگ با ایران، دیدار با رهبران چین و روسیه را موفقیت‌آمیز توصیف کرد و از احتمال دستیابی به توافقی برای پایان جنگ اوکراین سخن گفت. آقای ترامپ همچنین تهدید کرد که شرکت‌های آمریکایی را از ساخت مراکز داده هوش مصنوعی در خارج از آن کشور منع خواهد کرد.

دونالد ترامپ روز جمعه ۲۹ آبان (۲۰ نوامبر) در نشستی خبری در کاخ سفید گفت که قیمت بنزین پیش از آغاز عملیات نظامی آمریکا علیه ایران پایین بود و پیش‌بینی کرد که به‌زودی قیمت سوخت به میزان قابل‌توجهی کاهش یابد.

او گفت: «به‌زودی شاهد قیمت‌های بسیار، بسیار پایین خواهید بود. قیمت بنزین پیش از اقدام نظامی محدود آمریکا علیه ایران پایین بود.»

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا افزود: «قیمت بنزین از اینجا به بعد تا حدی به این بستگی دارد که تکلیف‌مان را با ایران چطور روشن کنیم.»

آقای ترامپ بار دیگر تکرار کرد که ایران خواهان توافق با آمریکاست، اما حاضر نیست توافقی را بپذیرد که از نظر او قابل قبول باشد.

او گفت: «ما می‌خواهیم به یک توافق واقعی برسیم، نه یک توافق ساختگی.»

آقای ترامپ همچنین مقام‌های جمهوری اسلامی را متهم کرد که طی ۵۱ سال گذشته دیگران را فریب داده‌اند.

اشاره او به ۵۱ سال سابقه رفتار حکومت ایران در حالی است که جمهوری اسلامی در سال ۱۳۵۷، یعنی ۴۷ سال پیش، تاسیس شد. رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا پیش‌تر نیز از عدد ۵۱ سال استفاده کرده، اما توضیح نداده است که مبدأ این محاسبه را چه رویدادی در نظر می‌گیرد.

در سال ۱۹۷۵، چهار سال پیش از انقلاب ایران، دو افسر نیروی هوایی آمریکا به نام‌های پل شفر و جک ترنر که در هیئت مستشاری نظامی آمریکا در ایران خدمت می‌کردند، در تهران ترور شدند. اسناد وزارت خارجه آمریکا این ترورها را به اعضای سازمان مجاهدین خلق نسبت داده‌اند. سازمان مجاهدین خلق این اتهام را رد کرده است.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا در بخش دیگری از این نشست، گزارش‌ها درباره نارضایتی خود از اظهارات جی‌دی ونس، معاونش، پس از شکست جمهوری‌خواهان در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای کنگره را رد کرد.

آقای ونس جنگ با ایران را از عوامل شکست جمهوری‌خواهان در این انتخابات دانسته بود.

آقای ترامپ گفت: «اتفاقاً بیانیه خوبی بود. قطعاً جنگ بر قیمت سوخت اثر گذاشت، اما بسیار کمتر از آنچه تصور می‌شد.»

او با دفاع دوباره از تصمیم خود برای آغاز جنگ با ایران افزود که این جنگ اجتناب‌ناپذیر بود و اگر به گذشته بازگردد، بار دیگر همان تصمیم را خواهد گرفت.

آقای ترامپ گفت: «من فکر می‌کردم قیمت نفت به ۳۰۰ دلار برای هر بشکه برسد، اما الان تقریباً به ۸۰ دلار برای هر بشکه رسیده است.»

رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا با اشاره به محاصره دریایی ایران، از نیروی دریایی و ارتش این کشور تشکر کرد و گفت آمریکا «کنترل کامل» تنگه هرمز را در اختیار دارد.

جنگ ایران و اختلال در کشتیرانی از تنگه هرمز طی ماه‌های گذشته بر بازار جهانی انرژی و قیمت سوخت تأثیر گذاشته است. تنگه هرمز یکی از مهم‌ترین گذرگاه‌های انتقال نفت و گاز جهان است.

آقای ترامپ در بخش دیگری از نشست خبری با اشاره به سرکوب اعتراضات دی‌ماه ۱۴۰۴ در ایران، اتهام‌های تندی را متوجه مقام‌های جمهوری اسلامی کرد.

news.originalContent:
Photo by Michael M. Santiago / Getty Images

Socialist Democratic New York mayor Zohran Mamdani announced his administration would be closing the second-largest jail in the U.S. for good.

Mamdani posted a one and a half minute video to X on Friday, announcing that Rikers Island — the more than 90-year-old 413-acre island jail complex in the East River — will be shut down by the end of 2032. This delays the timeline of the jail’s closure by five years as it was previously legally required to shutter by August 2027, according to CNN.

New York City Department of Correction Commissioner Stanley Richards, who appeared with Mamdani in the video announcement, was himself incarcerated at Rikers from 1986 to 1988 for robbery and drug activity, according to New York Daily News.

“At Rikers, out of sight and out of mind is the norm,” Richards said in the video.

“Our administration is closing Rikers Island, once and for all, and building a city where we ask ourselves what a person needs, not just what they’re accused of,” Mamdani chimed in.

Rikers currently holds over 6,600 inmates, according to New York City Jail Population Tracker. (RELATED: Mamdani Scraps NYPD Protest Unit, Here’s How Similar Moves Fueled BLM And Antifa Takeovers In Other Blue Cities)

We’re closing Rikers once and for all. https://t.co/VJieReQmSK

Rikers Island has earned the reputation with being one of the most violent jail systems in the country with high reports of inmates assaulting and stabbing each other and staff.

Kelly Rae Robertson a former corrections officer who served at Rikers Island for 15 years, detailed her experience working at the jail in an opinion piece for the Daily Caller in May.

“Shanked. Again and again. Officers were left bleeding out while alarms screamed and help was trapped somewhere else,” Robertson wrote. “On my way out after a shift, I stepped over pools of blood and passed walls smeared with it more times than I can count.”

Mamdani plans to bring the number of inmates in New York City down to about 4,500 spread amongst four borough-based jails starting in 2029, NBC reported.

The borough jails are expected to open in Brooklyn in 2029, the Bronx and Queens in 2031 and then Manhattan in 2032, according to City Hall. The new deadlines require approval from the New York City Council, the outlet said.

“Our city is safest when our government refuses to accept failed approaches to public safety just because it’s always been done this way,” Mamdani said. “We will work with the City Council, court partners, correctional staff and leaders at every level of government to make this a reality.”

Part of Mamdani’s plan is to build the jails closer to public transport “so New Yorkers can reach family, legal counsel, and court faster,” he said in the video.

Mamdani said he plans on building a criminal justice system that will “house thousands fewer New Yorkers,” and will “move people with serious mental health and medical issues from jails to hospitals,” announcing his administration will instate hundreds of therapeutic beds across NYC, the video shared.

“Dignity for everyone means safety for everyone,” the socialist mayor said.
