news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The unruly Arizona Realtor whose belligerent, racist outburst forced a Newark-bound flight to make an emergency landing had his state assault charges in Maryland dropped ahead of his trial.

Anne Arundel County prosecutors voluntarily dropped the second-degree assault and disorderly conduct charges against Arthur “Layne” Lundeen on Monday, claiming that the tantrum falls under federal jurisdiction, the Arizona Republic reported.

The state trial against Lundeen, 67, was expected to kick off Monday.

“Based on the fact that the alleged conduct currently charged took place in the air during flight, the State believes the matter falls under Federal jurisdiction,” an Anne Arundel County State Attorney’s spokesperson told the outlet.

Lundeen was indicted by a federal grand jury on Oct. 13 for interfering with a flight crew and assault resulting in the unplanned landing at Baltimore-Washington International airport, US Attorney for the District of Maryland Kelly O. Hayes announced.

The unruly passenger allegedly hurled racial slurs at a flight attendant and shouted anti-gay insults during his meltdown aboard American Airlines flight 618 from Dallas to Newark on Sept. 3.

Lundeen, a former Realtor in Tucson, is also accused of making physical contact with the flight attendant and engaging in disruptive and hostile behavior towards the flight crew.

Fellow passengers duct-taped and zip-tied Lundeen to his first-class seat until the flight made the premature landing in Baltimore.

Lundeen’s seatmate – controversial author and Messianic rabbi Jonathan Cahn – said the Realtor was cordial until he “became increasingly unruly.”

“I have never seen someone change in a split second from light to dark as I saw then, as if something had taken him over,” Cahn stated after the flight. “He went from the friendliest guy in the world to this dark person.”

Lundeen was fired from his job as vice president of Long Realty in Tucson, Ariz., after his viral arrest.

“Upon learning of the incident, Long Realty promptly ended its affiliation with the individual. The individual is no longer associated with or authorized to represent Long Realty in any capacity,” the company noted.

Lundeen claimed he didn’t remember any of the part of his mid-flight meltdown, adding he had two orange juice and vodka cocktails before his tirade.

“I don’t remember any of what happened,” he said during a court appearance in September, according to the Baltimore Banner.

“Oh my God. What a mess. I don’t remember any of it,” Lundeen muttered as the accusations against him were read.

Lundeen faces a maximum of 20 years in federal prison for interfering with the flight crew and an additional one year for assault if convicted.

These are a new piece of the NBA lexicon, and it looked like the Knicks were more than happy to explain. They are called “schedule losses,” and they can take several forms. The fourth game of a five-game West Coast trip. The last of a three-games-in-four-nights grind.

Or this: a second game in three nights, on the road, against the same team, a basketball series that borrows from baseball.

Sometimes, the reasoning goes, the unforgiving NBA schedule just deals you a bad hand. Deals you a built-in loss.

This felt like a built-in loss. Scottie Barnes knocked down a 7-footer, just over five minutes to go in the first half. That made it 48-35, Raptors. The Knicks looked tired. The Knicks looked sluggish. The Raptors couldn’t miss, not from 3, not around the basket. The Knicks haven’t been blown out all year. It felt headed that way. Felt like a schedule loss.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

A US Army lieutenant colonel suspected of spying for Russia was handed over to US military authorities Tuesday, days after British counterterrorism police arrested him on suspicion of violating national security laws.

Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, 41, was arrested Nov. 10 near Gloucester, England, on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service and obtaining or disclosing protected information under the United Kingdom’s National Security Act.

British authorities previously said the allegations involved Russia, which the Kremlin denied any connection to.

The Associated Press, citing a US official, reported that Tyner had not provided information to Russia.

Tyner’s transfer followed consultations between British prosecutors, the UK attorney general’s office and US authorities, according to London’s Metropolitan Police.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of UK’s Counter Terrorism Policing, said investigators referred the case to the Crown Prosecution Service, which consulted the attorney general’s office and US authorities before transferring the investigation.

“These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place,” Taylor said in a statement.

FBI Director Kash Patel said the officer was in custody following a joint espionage investigation involving the FBI’s Philadelphia field office, its London legal attaché office, British counterterrorism police, MI5, UK defense counterintelligence officials and US Army Counterintelligence Command.

“This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk. That’s been demonstrated by the 167 counterintelligence and espionage arrests we’ve made over the last 21 months, a 53% increase,” Patel said.

Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, commander of US Army Counterintelligence Command, warned service members against violating their oath to defend the Constitution.

“This case should serve as a stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath we all take to protect and defend the Constitution,” Stinchon said.

Tyner, who previously deployed to Afghanistan, Iraq and Qatar, served as a senior human resources officer with NATO’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps at Imjin Barracks near Gloucester.

The British-led multinational force, which includes personnel from 20 nations, is designed to respond rapidly to military crises and operations.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied Russian involvement following Tyner’s arrest, according to the AP.

“This arrest does not concern us in any way,” Peskov said Nov. 11. “We don’t know what it’s connected to. We have nothing to do with this.”

British police said Tyner’s arrest was unrelated to other ongoing counterterrorism investigations.

According to a Nov. 13 statement from the US Army, Tyner entered active-duty service in January 2008 and deployed to Afghanistan from December 2013 to December 2014, Qatar from July 2016 to July 2017, and Iraq from December 2019 to July 2020.

news.originalContent:
The nuclear watchdog chief is seen as technically competent, but questions remain about his plans for UN reform.

International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) chief Rafael Grossi is eyeing the position of United Nations secretary-general amid a tense race to replace Antonio Guterres.

The Argentinian nominee has finished second in the latest UN Security Council (UNSC) straw poll behind Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan, with nine “encourage” and four “discourage” votes and eight candidates still in the fray.

Grossi, 65, has earned admiration and criticism in equal measure for his IAEA tenure, defined by his hands-on approach to crisis diplomacy in active war zones, but also by accusations of partisanship, levelled against him, especially by Iran.

He is running on an agenda to reform the UN in a way seen as favourable to United States President Donald Trump and his political ally, Argentinian President Javier Milei.

But China and Russia – two of the five permanent UNSC members with veto power – are unlikely to back a candidate so closely aligned with Washington, analysts say, and a global civil society campaign is throwing its weight behind the selection of the first woman to lead the UN in the organisation’s 81-year history.

Grossi’s legacy at the IAEA and decades-long career as an Argentinian diplomat have cast him as a pragmatic crisis manager.

Since being appointed the UN nuclear watchdog’s director general in 2019, Grossi has been firmly in the front row in moments of international tension, including personally leading inspection teams to Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia and Chornobyl nuclear power plants after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Jan Wouters, professor of international law and international organisations at KU Leuven in Belgium, said Grossi has “transformed the technical watchdog into a highly visible, proactive, diplomatic actor”.

“[He] significantly elevated the agency’s global profile through constant shuttle diplomacy and direct engagement with world leaders,” Wouters told Al Jazeera.

In Ukraine, by “focusing on technical safety rather than territorial sovereignty, he successfully brokered eight localised ceasefires between Russia and Ukraine to allow critical plant repairs” during the war, he added.

However, Ezequiel Jimenez Martinez, adjunct professor at the Pompeu Fabra law faculty in Barcelona, Spain, said Grossi’s very active role has “angered” the veto-wielding Russia, which sees him as having overstepped his position as agency head.

To be elected to lead the UN, a candidate needs at least nine votes in favour from the 15-member UNSC while avoiding a veto from any of its five permanent members (P5) – China, France, Russia, the US, and the United Kingdom. The 193-member UN General Assembly (UNGC) then has to sign off on the final choice.

The race is coming down to the wire, as Guterres must leave his post on December 31.

While none of the P5 has publicly announced its preference, the South China Morning Post reported that Beijing has ruled out Grossi for being too close to Washington and would instead back Grynspan.

While Iran is not a member of the UNSC, it has also been vocal in its opposition to Grossi as UN secretary-general. Tehran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman, Esmaeil Baghaei, accused the IAEA this month of being overly influenced by the US and European countries in its “one-sided and biased reporting about Iran’s peaceful nuclear programme”.

The IAEA has estimated that Iran was holding 440.9kg (972lb) of uranium enriched to up to 60 percent before the June 2025 Israeli-US attacks on Iran’s nuclear facilities. While uranium must be enriched to 90 percent to become weapons-grade, the process becomes quick at 60 percent. The amount Tehran has would be enough, if enriched further, to build 10 nuclear weapons, according to the agency.

Jimenez Martinez said Grossi is likely to withstand the criticism, “because the majority of governors of the [IAEA] agree with his approach on Iran”.

“In the context of the UN, probably [this will lead to] a bit of fireworks, but I don’t think it will change many votes,” he said.

Grossi’s technical ability to lead the UN alone is unlikely to put him much ahead in the race, observers said. Candidates for the post of secretary-general must also be seen as defenders of the UN Charter and the UN’s international law and human rights instruments.

For this reason, support from the Argentinian president is seen as Grossi’s main liability. Milei has framed international institutions as threats to national sovereignty and individual liberty, describing the UN itself as “useless” and its diplomats as “fatally arrogant parasites”.

Since being elected president in 2023, Milei has reignited a longstanding dispute with the UK over the Falkland Islands, a British-administered territory over which Argentina claims sovereignty. Milei has told UN delegates that the principle of self-determination should not apply to the population of the islands, which Argentina calls Las Malvinas.

The Trump administration has also been a fierce critic of the UN, withdrawing Washington from key agencies, slashing UN funding and bypassing the body when it came to launching the war on Iran in February.

Jimenez Martinez said Grossi is seen as close to both Milei and Trump and as someone who could usher in a UN agenda aligned with their foreign policies.

“This will mean, in practice, a shrinking of the UN structure,” Jimenez Martinez said, including merging agencies and reorienting the body around security rather than development.

Grossi has called on world leaders to have the “courage to reform” the institution and lead it into a new era. According to Jimenez Martinez, his insistence on cutting red tape while failing to elaborate on safeguards is unlikely to get him a green light from the UNGA.

Alvina Hoffmann, senior lecturer in diplomatic studies at SOAS University of London, said Grossi is widely seen as a candidate whose “emphasis is on improving the system and cutting overlapping mandates, rather than addressing the structural drivers of inequality”.

He is also seen as someone who focuses on personal leadership, confidential negotiations and preventive diplomacy, “rather than issuing public declarations or condemnations”, which “might come at the expense of being able to call out violations of international law at a time in which international law is increasingly under attack”, Hoffmann said.

According to the tradition of geographical rotation, the UN secretary-general post should next go to a Latin American. Five women are running in the race, and public and civil society pressure is at an all-time high to elect the first woman to the post.

Grynspan ticks both boxes.

Ben Donaldson, adviser to the 1 for 8 Billion campaign, a civil society movement advocating for the appointment of the first female secretary-general, said that while electing the next UN chief should be based on merit, this criterion “is not inconsistent with gender considerations”.

UNGA “resolutions and international standards affirm that due regard should be given to achieving gender balance in senior UN leadership”, Donaldson told Al Jazeera.

“In applying these principles, member states should assess candidates not only on their individual competencies and experience, but also on how their personal characteristics and professional trajectories contribute to a leadership that reflects the diversity of the international community.”

“The United Nations has existed for 80 years without ever appointing a woman as secretary-general,” he added. “This persistent imbalance stands in contrast to the organisation’s own commitments to equality, parity and nondiscrimination.”

“In the context of the UN, probably [this will lead to] a bit of fireworks, but I don’t think it will change many votes,” he said.

Grossi’s technical ability to lead the UN alone is unlikely to put him much ahead in the race, observers said. Candidates for the post of secretary-general must also be seen as defenders of the UN Charter and the UN’s international law and human rights instruments.

For this reason, support from the Argentinian president is seen as Grossi’s main liability. Milei has framed international institutions as threats to national sovereignty and individual liberty, describing the UN itself as “useless” and its diplomats as “fatally arrogant parasites”.

Since being elected president in 2023, Milei has reignited a longstanding dispute with the UK over the Falkland Islands, a British-administered territory over which Argentina claims sovereignty. Milei has told UN delegates that the principle of self-determination should not apply to the population of the islands, which Argentina calls Las Malvinas.

The Trump administration has also been a fierce critic of the UN, withdrawing Washington from key agencies, slashing UN funding and bypassing the body when it came to launching the war on Iran in February.

Jimenez Martinez said Grossi is seen as close to both Milei and Trump and as someone who could usher in a UN agenda aligned with their foreign policies.

“This will mean, in practice, a shrinking of the UN structure,” Jimenez Martinez said, including merging agencies and reorienting the body around security rather than development.

Grossi has called on world leaders to have the “courage to reform” the institution and lead it into a new era. According to Jimenez Martinez, his insistence on cutting red tape while failing to elaborate on safeguards is unlikely to get him a green light from the UNGA.

Alvina Hoffmann, senior lecturer in diplomatic studies at SOAS University of London, said Grossi is widely seen as a candidate whose “emphasis is on improving the system and cutting overlapping mandates, rather than addressing the structural drivers of inequality”.

He is also seen as someone who focuses on personal leadership, confidential negotiations and preventive diplomacy, “rather than issuing public declarations or condemnations”, which “might come at the expense of being able to call out violations of international law at a time in which international law is increasingly under attack”, Hoffmann said.

According to the tradition of geographical rotation, the UN secretary-general post should next go to a Latin American. Five women are running in the race, and public and civil society pressure is at an all-time high to elect the first woman to the post.

Grynspan ticks both boxes.

Ben Donaldson, adviser to the 1 for 8 Billion campaign, a civil society movement advocating for the appointment of the first female secretary-general, said that while electing the next UN chief should be based on merit, this criterion “is not inconsistent with gender considerations”.

UNGA “resolutions and international standards affirm that due regard should be given to achieving gender balance in senior UN leadership”, Donaldson told Al Jazeera.

“In applying these principles, member states should assess candidates not only on their individual competencies and experience, but also on how their personal characteristics and professional trajectories contribute to a leadership that reflects the diversity of the international community.”

“The United Nations has existed for 80 years without ever appointing a woman as secretary-general,” he added. “This persistent imbalance stands in contrast to the organisation’s own commitments to equality, parity and nondiscrimination.”

news.originalContent:
A look at FIFA’s presidential election process, the challengers and key dates, as Gianni Infantino seeks a fourth term.

The race for next year’s FIFA presidential election has entered a decisive phase this week, with candidates rushing to submit their nominations ahead of the deadline on Wednesday.

Incumbent Gianni Infantino is seeking a fourth term as the head of world football’s governing body, but many in the sport’s fraternity oppose his re-election following his now-aborted plan to sell stakes in future World Cups to private investors.

Standing in Infantino’s way are three challengers: French Football Federation chief Philippe Diallo, top Japanese football official Kozo Tashima, and Ramon Vega, an ex-Switzerland player.

Al Jazeera breaks down everything you need to know about the FIFA presidency and its upcoming elections:

The FIFA president is the primary representative and ceremonial head of the International Federation of Association Football (FIFA), serving as the lead figure for football’s global governing body.

The president holds the highest position in FIFA’s organisational chart, above the general secretary.

Infantino has been in power since February 2016, succeeding his compatriot Sepp Blatter, who resigned in June 2015. FIFA’s ethics committee had banned Blatter from the sport for eight years for a conflict of interest and disloyalty to the organisation over a $2m payment deal.

In its 122-year history, FIFA has never had a woman as its president. The highest administrative position held by a woman at FIFA was the secretary-general post in 2016, held by Fatma Samoura, a Senegalese diplomat and former United Nations official.

The next election will be held at the 77th FIFA Congress on March 18, 2027, in Rabat, Morocco.

FIFA holds its presidential elections every four years, staging them at its congress that follows a men’s World Cup – in this case, the 2026 World Cup in North America, won by Spain.

A candidate wins the election based on the backing of individual member nations across six confederations.

There are 211 FIFA member nations. Each holds equal weight in the vote and can support only one candidate per election.

If two candidates are contesting the election, a simple majority of more than 50 percent is needed to win – which translates to the support of 106 member nations.

If there are more than two candidates, a two-thirds majority is required in the first round. Further rounds of voting are held, and the candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated each time. This continues until only two candidates remain, and from there on, the candidate with a simple majority wins.

Each member nation in a confederation has one vote. The breakdown of the six confederations’ votes is as follows:

Candidates require the backing of five national associations to stand in the election, and four men are in the running for the next FIFA president.

Infantino is the highest-profile candidate. The 56-year-old Swiss administrator is seeking a fourth term through 2031.

His closest challenger is Frenchman Diallo, who has the “unanimous” backing of the European national associations. The 63-year-old, the son of a Senegalese boxing champion, has been president of the French Football Federation since January 2023.

Japan has fielded a candidate for the first time in history, with Tashima, the Japan Football Association’s (JFA) honorary president, challenging Infantino.

Former Japan international Tashima, who has served on the FIFA Council since 2015 and became JFA president the following year, believes he has a 20- to 30-percent chance of winning the coveted seat in global football.

The list of candidates wraps up with ex-Tottenham Hotspur centre-back Vega, the first to publicly declare his intention to challenge fellow Swiss citizen Infantino.

Arsene Wenger, a French former Arsenal manager and FIFA’s current chief of global football development, had been seen as a potential candidate to get Europe’s backing.

The AFP news agency reported that Wenger had been UEFA’s “Plan A” and that Diallo had never been seen as a solution before it became clear the ex-Arsenal boss would not be a candidate.

CONCACAF chief Victor Montagliani had also been mooted as a candidate, but the Canadian later announced his desire to stand for a new term as the head of his confederation, which covers North and Central America and the Caribbean.

In July, Infantino faced furious worldwide backlash after an unsuccessful attempt to bring private investors into a proposed FIFA commercial entity that would hold rights linked to competitions, including the World Cup.

UEFA, CONCACAF, and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) led the opposition to Infantino and his plan, signing a letter saying football “belongs to no individual”.

But the AFC later performed a U-turn, throwing its weight behind Infantino, who has since apologised for the failed private investment project.

Opposition from UEFA, whose member associations account for 55 votes, and CONCACAF, with 35 votes, could cause minor problems in Infantino’s re-election bid.

UEFA had been struggling to find a credible candidate to stand against Infantino, naming Diallo only two days before the official nomination deadline.

Earlier this month, Miguel ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Maduro, the former head of FIFA’s governance committee, said Infantino cannot stand for ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌a fourth term as president under the organisation’s statutes.

“Article 33, paragraph two of the FIFA statutes is very clear when it says no person may serve as president for more than three terms,” Maduro told reporters.

“Gianni Infantino has been elected three times; he’s ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌been president of FIFA for three terms. So, in my view, there’s no way to reconcile another presidency of Infantino.”

Human rights organisation FairSquare also wrote to member associations urging them to declare Infantino ineligible. FairSquare had previously urged FIFA to rule that Infantino was ineligible to seek another term, arguing he has already served ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠the maximum three permitted under the body’s statutes.

But Infantino successfully argued that his first spell in charge, when he was elected at an Extraordinary Congress in 2016 following Blatter’s resignation, should not count towards that limit because it completed an interrupted ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠mandate.

In December 2022, the FIFA Council “unanimously confirmed” that the period between 2016 and 2019 does not count as a term of office for Infantino, but FairSquare said the reasoning was never made public.

Infantino’s re-election ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠prospects have strengthened significantly in recent weeks.

Last month, the head of Asian football endorsed his bid in a dramatic change of heart, while ⁠⁠⁠support across confederations gives him a commanding position among FIFA’s 211 voting members.

Infantino believes he has the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of member associations, despite criticism of his World Cup sell-off plan.

“I think what is important is that in an organisation like FIFA, there can be different views, different points of view,” Infantino told the BBC.

“But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone, if we are serious about that, then we need to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority.

“I’m just coming back off Tokyo, where the Asian Football Confederation has fully endorsed me. I was in Cape Verde, where all African countries have endorsed me. I’m speaking to all associations everywhere in the world,” he added.

“There are different points of view; it’s not always easy to bring them all under one roof, but we need to respect – and I do respect – all opinions and all views, and then it will be up to the FIFA member associations to decide who they want as a president and how they want FIFA to be run.”

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Robert Pattinson has apparently conquered Hollywood, and now he’s coming for your paycheck next.

The 40-year-old actor’s reported casting as the next James Bond in director Denis Villeneuve’s upcoming 007 film has unleashed an internet meme frenzy, with social media users joking that Pattinson isn’t satisfied stealing every major role in Hollywood. Now he wants every job on the planet.

Batman? Check. Twilight, Harry Potter and Dune? Been there, done that. Christopher Nolan’s Odyssey? Duh. James Bond? Add it to the résumé.

Apparently, there’s no such thing as a hiring freeze when Robert Pattinson submits an application.

AI won’t take my job.  Robert Pattinson will

“If you have job rn it’s because Robert Pattinson doesn’t want it,” one X user joked.

Another feared showing up to work only to discover Pattinson already sitting at their desk.

Even KFC Spain joined the unemployment line, joking that Pattinson had taken every available position, including the person running its social media account.

The internet even announced that Pattinson was taking over as the new CEO of NVIDIA in the wake of the Jensen Huang cheating scandal.

BREAKING: Robert Pattison has been selected by Nvidia’s board as the new CEO, effective immediately. pic.twitter.com/jOXeySbQ65

Robert Pattinson has been cast as Nicholas Hoult in upcoming biopic pic.twitter.com/PqNvDrdeNF

Perhaps the funniest meme involves actor Nicholas Hoult, who reportedly lost out on playing Batman to Pattinson. Naturally, the internet cast Pattinson as Hoult in a fictional biopic about losing the James Bond role to, well, Robert Pattinson.

But the best memes have invaded the sports world, where apparently no athlete’s contract is safe.

The Chargers have a new quarterback, and his name isn’t Justin Herbert. It’s Robert Pattinson.

BREAKING: Robert Pattinson will start over Justin Herbert tonight, with coach Jim Harbaugh quoted saying, “My job is to put my team in the best position to win a ballgame.” pic.twitter.com/C87xCccoEW

REPORT: The Patriots are naming Robert Pattinson their starting QB for the rest of the season pic.twitter.com/uAm5PxfgIq

The Philadelphia Eagles have apparently found their next franchise quarterback, while the New England Patriots have identified Pattinson as the perfect replacement for injured starter Drake Maye.

Baseball isn’t safe, either. The Atlanta Braves have reportedly found their bullpen savior.

BREAKING: #Braves are signing utility man Robert Pattinson to a five-year deal worth $100 millionTurns out he truly can do every job #BravesCountry #LANK pic.twitter.com/T9uSrwIXD5

BREAKING NEWS: Robert Pattinson signs as a RubberDuck. He will be playing the role of RubberDucks star player for the 2027 season. #QuAkron #Satire pic.twitter.com/aGGGLmlElx

OFFICIAL: Lakers sign Robert Pattinson to a two-way contract. pic.twitter.com/SXUIbJ9r7A

While the Akron RubberDucks, Cleveland’s Double-A affiliate, have joined the Pattinson sweepstakes.

And with Austin Reaves and Austin Kessler sidelined, the Lakers have apparently signed Pattinson to a two-way contract.

At this rate, the only person guaranteed job security is Pattinson’s agent.

news.originalContent:
California authorities have declared self-driving cars an ‘imminent hazard to public safety’ after traffic incidents.

Waymo has paused its driverless taxi services on freeways across the United States after California temporarily banned the ride-hailing platform on the state’s highways over safety concerns.

A spokesperson for the California-based company – a subsidiary of Alphabet, Google’s parent company – said it has “temporarily restricted commercial freeway rides in all markets where we operate that service”, but it is “continuing freeway testing with trained autonomous specialists behind the wheel”.

Waymo implemented the suspension last Wednesday, according to the spokesperson, but they did not say how long it would last.

Along with California, the driverless vehicles will pause highway services in Phoenix, Austin and Miami. Waymo offers rides on city streets in areas including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver.

The spokesperson said the suspension would allow the company to “evaluate our performance” following incidents in California and that it prioritises safety.

One incident on November 6 went viral after video captured on a San Francisco highway showed a Waymo vehicle speeding towards and attempting to pass two police cars, even as their lights were flashing in an intentional bid to slow traffic.

The officers were driving behind a slow-moving construction truck.

Waymo completes half a million trips each week and says it has demonstrated a 95 percent reduction in serious crashes as compared with human-driven vehicles.

news.originalContent:
Senators berated acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao on Tuesday for framing suicide attempts by sailors under his watch as mere “mitigations.”

The exchange, now gaining traction online, took place during a Senate confirmation hearing for the official Secretary of the Navy position, during which Cao faced a gauntlet of lawmakers who pressed him on his and President Donald Trump’s decision to carry on the administration’s war with Iran. (RELATED: Pentagon Can’t Pass An Audit, Wants $1.5 Trillion From Taxpayers)

Democratic New York Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand raised Cao’s dismissal of August reports that conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln after nearly nine months of uninterrupted deployment had led to eight suicide attempts.

At the time, Cao called the report “dishonest,” saying the media was “trying to paint our warriors as victims.” On Tuesday, he reaffirmed his position and said he had spoken to sailors on the ship who felt the same.

.@SenGillibrand (D-NY) and Navy secretary nominee Hung Cao have heated exchange about suicide attempts on USS Abraham Lincoln including one sailor who jumped overboard: Cao: "That sailor was not trying to kill himself…" Gillibrand: "What was he trying to do? Swim to Guam?" https://t.co/ARJQf07hO3

Gillibrand also pointed to the deployment’s piping failures, rationed hygiene supplies, and eight suicide attempts, including one in which a service member attempted to jump overboard.

“Well, Senator, again, these are eight mitigations we’re able to mitigate…” Cao said, trying to frame the unsuccessful suicide attempts as operational success before being cut off by Gillibrand.

“Please don’t call attempted suicide mitigations! That is such an insult,” the senator interjected. “It’s an insult to these men and women who are devoting their lives to the armed services. When you say it’s mitigation, you’re compartmentalizing something that is clearly a mental health failure. The fact that a service member, a sailor, went overboard is beyond a mitigation. It is an attempted suicide that, but for the grace of God, was unsuccessful.”

“Senator, that sailor was not trying to kill himself, and he admitted that. He admitted that to the committee…” Cao responded before being cut off by Gillibrand again.

“What was he trying to do, swim to Guam?!” she asked.

Republican presidential nominee, former U.S. President Donald Trump speaks alongside Republican candidate for U.S. Senate in Virginia Hung Cao at the Truong Tien Restaurant in the Eden Center on August 26, 2024 in Falls Church, Virginia. (Photo by Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

In defense, the nominee said the sailor was not trying to kill himself but had jumped overboard wearing a life preserver in what the sailor would later describe to a commanding officer as an attempt to “get out of there.”

Gillibrand suggested the sailor said that to minimize any discipline that would result from the action. “I think you are minimizing the mental health strain that is on these service workers,” she continued, calling his framing “inadequate.”

Cao responded by pointing to the terrible conditions he had faced while deployed in the past, including very limited food and water.

“I understand what our sailors and Marines are going through, and I put mental health as top of my concerns,” Cao said. “I’ve really worked a lot to mitigate mental health concerns and mitigated a lot of suicides.”

Cao also pointed to the efforts of mental health resiliency providers and chaplains on board while suggesting more funding would be needed to further their effectiveness.

Calling the effort “inadequate,” Gillibrand ignored the request for additional funding and suggested a future hearing on mental health and stability.

Cao raised the need for funding again, and the senator responded, “You need to do better for our service member if you want to be secretary of the Navy.”

🚨 JUST IN: Trump Navy Secretary nominee Hung Cao just DROPPED this response at insufferable Sen. Elizabeth Warren CAO: Losing the Strait is even worse. WARREN: The blockade costs $32.5M a day! CAO: Let me do some quick Asian math in my head. About $30B so far. WARREN: *Keeps raging* This patriot is keeping his composure under one of the most angry and deranged Senators in Congress! Confirm him NOW!

But that wasn’t the only heated exchange of the hearing. Democratic Massachusetts Sen. Elizabeth Warren pressed the nominee on the cost of the war, pointing out that the money could have gone toward health care or paying off student loans.

Cao was not able to share the daily monetary cost of the blockade on Iran and instead attempted to point to what America would lose if the Strait of Hormuz were surrendered to Iran before being cut off by Warren.

“I’m not asking you that; I just want to have the dollars here,” the senator said, suggesting independent estimates place the cost of the blockade at $32.5 million a day.

When asked if the number sounded “about right,” Cao volunteered to do some “quick asian math in my head,” before Warren moved on.

“How many Americans’ federal student loans could we wipe out with the $47 billion that we have already spent on this war?” Warren asked.

“Senator, if we didn’t have the blockade…” Cao tried to say before Warren said that 200 million students could have had their student loans paid. (RELATED: US Deploys Third Aircraft Carrier As Iran War Stretches Navy To Its Limits)

Voting on Cao’s confirmation as Secretary of the Navy has not yet been scheduled.

news.originalContent:
(Getty Images/Kevin Carter)

The United States has deployed a third aircraft carrier to the Middle East as the war with Iran heats up, bolstering American naval firepower amid renewed Iranian attacks and mounting fears of another major military confrontation.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt and its accompanying warships have entered the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) area of responsibility, joining the USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington as President Donald Trump weighs renewed military action against Tehran, according to an X post made by CENTCOM. The growing American naval presence comes as Iran launches fresh drone attacks against U.S. military installations in Bahrain, threatens shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and refuses to allow international nuclear inspections while diplomatic efforts to end the eight-month war remain stalled.

CENTCOM declined to comment to the Daily Caller News Foundation. (RELATED: Trump Backs $350 Billion Reconciliation Bill Lavishing More Spending On Defense Industry)

The Iran War shows no signs of stopping, with Qatari-brokered peace efforts reaching a standstill on Nov. 9 due to Iran’s requests. Iran then attacked an installation via drone by America’s largest Middle East Navy base on Friday, Nov 13.

USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN 71) sails with USS George Washington (CVN 73) in the Arabian Sea, Nov. 17. https://t.co/KCP22Iikx1

Approximately 9,000-10,000 military personnel are deployed with the USS Theodore Roosevelt strike group, according to the Washington Post.

The Iran War has put tremendous strain on the Navy, with deployments now being extended.

“You can kind of expect at least a 10-month deployment, and so that’s just the nature of what the capacity of the Navy can do,” Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle told USNI News in October.

This announcement followed the return of the USS Abraham Lincoln, where eight sailors tried to kill themselves during its long deployment.

Most recently, Acting Secretary of the Navy, Hung Cao, faced pushback from family members at a town hall at Naval Station Norfolk when he told them that the USS George HW Bush would not be home for the holidays. Military family members expressed their frustrations at the extended deployments, substandard quality of living that sailors were subjected to, and lack of mental health services.

“Trust within the force and among our families is heavily strained right now between record-breaking stretches without relief, shifting timelines and the feeling that communication downplays the reality on the ground. Families are burning out under the immense strain,” one family member said.

news.title: واژگونی اتوبوس در ایلام؛ تجمع اعتراضی در آبدانان
news.originalSummary:
گزارش‌ها و ویدئوهای منتشرشده در شبکه‌های اجتماعی از تجمع مردم در آبدانان در اعتراض به قصور مسئولان پس از واژگونی مرگبار اتوبوس خبر می‌دهند. در همین حال دادستان آبدانان می‌گوید علیه مدیرعامل ان‌جی‌ال و مدیرکل راهداری استان ایلام اعلام جرم کرده است.

گزارش‌ها و ویدئوهای منتشرشده در شبکه‌های اجتماعی از تجمع مردم در آبدانان در اعتراض به قصور مسئولان پس از واژگونی مرگبار اتوبوس خبر می‌دهند. در همین حال دادستان آبدانان می‌گوید علیه مدیرعامل ان‌جی‌ال و مدیرکل راهداری استان ایلام اعلام جرم کرده است.

در این حادثه ۱۳ نفر کشته و ۱۷ نفر مصدوم شدند.

اتوبوس سرویس ایاب‌وذهاب کارکنان شیفت بهره‌برداری شرکت اویکو در مجموعه ‌ان‌جی‌ال دهلران شامگاه شنبه ۲۳ آبان در مسیر دشت‌عباس دهلران به مورموری آبدانان در حرکت بود که در محدوده سه‌گر واژگون شد.

مجروحان به بیمارستان آبدانان منتقل شدند و ویدئوهایی از تجمع مردم در مقابل بیمارستان بعد از حادثه منتشر شد.

در منطقه برای این تصادف مرگبار عزای عمومی اعلام شد.

خبرگزاری فارس در گزارشی از «تجمع اعتراضی در آبدانان در پی حادثه واژگونی اتوبوس شرکت ان‌جی‌ال» نوشت که این تجمع ساعاتی پیش در میدان ولی‌عصر آغاز شد و «معترضان با شعار عزاست امروز و استعفا استعفا خواستار برخورد با عاملان این حادثه شدند.»

این خبرگزاری که به نهادهای امنیتی نزدیک است نوشت: «پس از دقایقی، با میدان‌داری برخی افراد، جمعیت از میدان ولی‌عصر به سمت خیابان‌های دیگر حرکت کرد و شعارها نیز در مواردی رنگ‌وبوی سیاسی به خود گرفت.»

بنابر این گزارش، «در جریان حرکت، برخی نفرات تلاش کردند که به اموال عمومی آسیب برسانند و دیگر حاضران را که بیشتر تماشاگر بودند تحریک و تهییج کنند اما اکثریت حضار با این اقدامات همراهی نکردند. نیروهای پلیس نیز برای کنترل شرایط در محل حاضر شده‌اند.»

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

امراله میسائی دادستان عمومی و انقلاب شهرستان آبدانان امروز گفت که پس از انجام تحقیقات و کارشناسی دقیق، علیه مدیرعامل ان‌جی‌ال دهلران و مدیرکل راهداری استان ایلام اعلام جرم شد.

او همچنین با اشاره به تجمع اعتراضی در آبدانان گفت که با افرادی که از حادثه  «سواستفاده می‌کنند» و «قصد بر هم زدن نظم عمومی و تحریک احساسات مردم را داشته باشند با قاطعیت» برخورد خواهد کرد.

در همین حال، خبرگزاری رسمی دولت ایران (ایرنا) هم تجمع اعتراضی آبدانان را «غیرقانونی» خواند و آن را به فراخوان «عناصر خارج‌نشین» نسبت داد.

گزارش شده کارشناسان پلیس راه سهم تقصیر را میان راننده، شرکت پیمانکار حمل‌ونقل و اداره راهداری تقسیم کرده‌اند.

دادستان آبدانان می‌گوید «قطعا مطالبات خانواده جانباختگان حادثه با دقت پیگیری می‌شود» و وعده داد که با مقصران برخورد خواهد کرد.

در همین حال گزارش شده که مدیرعامل پتروپالایش دهلران و مدیر مجتمع ان‌جی‌ال پتروپالایش دهلران از سمت‌هایشان عزل شده‌اند.

گزارش شده که مدیریت هلدینگ اهداف که پتروپالایش دهلران از زیرمجموعه‌های آن است تصمیم به برکناری مدیرعامل این شرکت گرفته است.

پتروپالایش دهلران در بخش جمع‌آوری و فرآورش گازهای همراه نفت فعالیت می‌کند.

رئیس پلیس راه استان ایلام گفت: «با بررسی دقیق فنی و حقوقی حادثه واژگونی اتوبوس در محور دشت عباس آبدانان، جزئیات عوامل دخیل در این واقعه را در سه محور اصلی شناسایی شدند.»

به گزارش رسانه‌های ایران، سرهنگ کامران آرمان گفت: «نخستین عامل بروز حادثه، خطای انسانی و بی‌احتیاطی راننده اتوبوس (برند ولوو) بوده است.»

این گزارش‌ها حاکیست که «بر اساس بررسی‌های انجام شده، عدم توانایی راننده در کنترل وسیله نقلیه ناشی از تخطی از سرعت.»

سرهنگ آرمان گفت: «محور دوم، به تخلفات ساختاری شرکت بهره‌بردار اشاره دارد. این شرکت با تنظیم قراردادهای اجاره مغایر با ضوابط و مقررات حمل‌ونقل عمومی مسافر، در حوزه خدمات سرویس دربستی فعالیت می‌کرده است.»

رئیس پلیس راه استان ایلام بخش سوم بررسی ها را مربوط به «نقص در تجهیزات ایمنی مسیر» دانست و «عدم نصب حفاظ طولی مناسب در این بخش از جاده.»

رئیس پلیس راه استان ایلام گفت: «با بررسی دقیق فنی و حقوقی حادثه واژگونی اتوبوس در محور دشت عباس آبدانان، جزئیات عوامل دخیل در این واقعه را در سه محور اصلی شناسایی شدند.»

گزارش‌ها و ویدئوهای منتشرشده در شبکه‌های اجتماعی از تجمع مردم در آبدانان در اعتراض به قصور مسئولان پس از واژگونی مرگبار اتوبوس خبر می‌دهند. در همین حال دادستان آبدانان می‌گوید علیه مدیرعامل ان‌جی‌ال و مدیرکل راهداری استان ایلام اعلام جرم کرده است.

در این حادثه ۱۳ نفر کشته و ۱۷ نفر مصدوم شدند.

اتوبوس سرویس ایاب‌وذهاب کارکنان شیفت بهره‌برداری شرکت اویکو در مجموعه ‌ان‌جی‌ال دهلران شامگاه شنبه ۲۳ آبان در مسیر دشت‌عباس دهلران به مورموری آبدانان در حرکت بود که در محدوده سه‌گر واژگون شد.

مجروحان به بیمارستان آبدانان منتقل شدند و ویدئوهایی از تجمع مردم در مقابل بیمارستان بعد از حادثه منتشر شد.

در منطقه برای این تصادف مرگبار عزای عمومی اعلام شد.

خبرگزاری فارس در گزارشی از «تجمع اعتراضی در آبدانان در پی حادثه واژگونی اتوبوس شرکت ان‌جی‌ال» نوشت که این تجمع ساعاتی پیش در میدان ولی‌عصر آغاز شد و «معترضان با شعار عزاست امروز و استعفا استعفا خواستار برخورد با عاملان این حادثه شدند.»

این خبرگزاری که به نهادهای امنیتی نزدیک است نوشت: «پس از دقایقی، با میدان‌داری برخی افراد، جمعیت از میدان ولی‌عصر به سمت خیابان‌های دیگر حرکت کرد و شعارها نیز در مواردی رنگ‌وبوی سیاسی به خود گرفت.»

بنابر این گزارش، «در جریان حرکت، برخی نفرات تلاش کردند که به اموال عمومی آسیب برسانند و دیگر حاضران را که بیشتر تماشاگر بودند تحریک و تهییج کنند اما اکثریت حضار با این اقدامات همراهی نکردند. نیروهای پلیس نیز برای کنترل شرایط در محل حاضر شده‌اند.»

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

امراله میسائی دادستان عمومی و انقلاب شهرستان آبدانان امروز گفت که پس از انجام تحقیقات و کارشناسی دقیق، علیه مدیرعامل ان‌جی‌ال دهلران و مدیرکل راهداری استان ایلام اعلام جرم شد.

او همچنین با اشاره به تجمع اعتراضی در آبدانان گفت که با افرادی که از حادثه  «سواستفاده می‌کنند» و «قصد بر هم زدن نظم عمومی و تحریک احساسات مردم را داشته باشند با قاطعیت» برخورد خواهد کرد.

news.originalContent:
(Getty Images/Kevin Carter)

The Pentagon has failed its ninth consecutive financial audit despite overseeing trillions in taxpayer-funded assets, as the Trump administration pushes for a record $1.5 trillion defense budget.

The Department of War (DoW) failed to obtain a clean audit of its $4.9 trillion in assets and $5.2 trillion in liabilities, continuing a nearly decade-long streak of financial accountability failures, The Hill reported Tuesday. The latest failure comes as Secretary of War Pete Hegseth seeks a 44% increase in military spending, which would push the total $1.5 trillion, according to the Government Accountability Office.

Hegseth’s request stands despite longstanding concerns over the Pentagon’s outdated accounting systems, financial mismanagement and vulnerability to waste, fraud and abuse.

The @DeptofWar will pass a full, clean audit by 2028. We are more than halfway there — huge, historic progress so far. We owe it to American taxpayers. 👇

The DoW did not immediately respond to the Daily Caller News Foundation’s request for comment. (RELATED: The Deep State Is Leaking Trump’s Most Sensitive Undercover Operations To The Washington Post)

The audit included nearly 30 Pentagon components and 1,500 auditors from the Department of War Inspector General (DoW OIG), according to a DoW OIG press release.

“For fiscal year (FY) 2026, the DoW OIG issued a disclaimer of opinion which means the DoW management could not provide sufficient evidence to the auditors to support an opinion on the reliability of the financial statements,” the release read.

Hegseth has set the goal of a clean audit by 2028. To help with that, he has formed an audit committee, the Hill reported.

“Although the number of material weaknesses appears lower in FY 2026, that reduction stems from consolidation, not resolution,” Brett Mansfield, Deputy Inspector General for Audit said in the press release.

منبع تصویر، hammihanonline

دادستان عمومی و انقلاب مرکز استان کرمانشاه از بازداشت پدر سوگند صیادی و مدیر مدرسه این دانش‌آموز ۱۶ ساله خبر داد.

به گزارش میزان، خبرگزاری قوه قضائیه، حمیدرضا کریمی، دادستان عمومی و انقلاب مرکز استان کرمانشاه، گفت: «در ادامه تحقیقات قضایی و با توجه به شواهد و مستندات موجود، پدر این دانش‌آموز در ارتباط با اتهامات مطرح‌شده از جمله ضرب‌وجرح و فعلا قتل و مدیر مدرسه نیز به دلیل قصور و سهل‌انگاری مرتبط با موضوع، امروز بازداشت شدند.»

آقای کریمی همچنین گفت که «تا پیش از تکمیل تحقیقات و اعلام نتایج بررسی‌های کارشناسی، نمی‌توان درباره علت قطعی فوت اظهارنظر کرد» و «فرضیه‌های مختلف از جمله قتل یا خودکشی با جدیت در حال بررسی است.»

خبر فوت یک دختر ۱۶ ساله در کرمانشاه را دیروز ابتدا خبرگزاری رکنا منتشر کرد و گفت که پلیس و آموزش‌وپرورش تحقیق و بررسی در این باره را آغاز کرده‌اند.

خبرگزاری رکنا در این باره از مدیر روابط عمومی آموزش‌وپرورش کرمانشاه سوال کرده بود.

آقای آقایی گفته بود: «طبق اطلاعاتی که از مدیر مدرسه دریافت کرده‌ایم، پدر سوگند یک روز پیش از حادثه به مدرسه مراجعه و درخواست دریافت پرونده تحصیلی او را مطرح کرده است. با این حال، مدیر مدرسه موظف است پرونده دانش‌آموز را تنها در صورت انتقال او به مدرسه‌ای دیگر تحویل دهد و در صورت قصد ترک تحصیل، اجازه تحویل پرونده را ندارد.»

او همچنین گفت: «ظاهرا سوگند برای بازگشت به شهرستان تحت فشار بوده است اما اینکه پس از بازگشت به خانه چه اتفاقاتی رخ داده، هنوز مشخص نیست. برای روشن شدن ابعاد ماجرا باید با پدر و نامادری این دانش‌آموز گفت‌وگو شود و تمام این موارد در دست بررسی است.»

رکنا یک فایل صوتی هم منتشر کرد که در آن فردی که گفته شد از دوستان سوگند است، می‌گوید او پیش از رفتن به خانه گفته بود: «اگر به خانه بروم، پدرم من را می‌کشد.»

به گزارش رکنا، «بر اساس اطلاعات دریافتی از منابع محلی، روز ۲۳ آبان‌ماه، از مدرسه موضوعی را با عنوان علت ارتباط شخصی به پدر سوگند اطلاع می‌دهند. گفته می‌شود پس از این اتفاق، پدر سوگند حدود ساعت ۸:۴۵ صبح به مدرسه مراجعه کرده و دخترش را با خود به خانه می‌برد.»

منبع تصویر، hammihanonline

دادستان عمومی و انقلاب مرکز استان کرمانشاه از بازداشت پدر سوگند صیادی و مدیر مدرسه این دانش‌آموز ۱۶ ساله خبر داد.

به گزارش میزان، خبرگزاری قوه قضائیه، حمیدرضا کریمی، دادستان عمومی و انقلاب مرکز استان کرمانشاه، گفت: «در ادامه تحقیقات قضایی و با توجه به شواهد و مستندات موجود، پدر این دانش‌آموز در ارتباط با اتهامات مطرح‌شده از جمله ضرب‌وجرح و فعلا قتل و مدیر مدرسه نیز به دلیل قصور و سهل‌انگاری مرتبط با موضوع، امروز بازداشت شدند.»

آقای کریمی همچنین گفت که «تا پیش از تکمیل تحقیقات و اعلام نتایج بررسی‌های کارشناسی، نمی‌توان درباره علت قطعی فوت اظهارنظر کرد» و «فرضیه‌های مختلف از جمله قتل یا خودکشی با جدیت در حال بررسی است.»

خبر فوت یک دختر ۱۶ ساله در کرمانشاه را دیروز ابتدا خبرگزاری رکنا منتشر کرد و گفت که پلیس و آموزش‌وپرورش تحقیق و بررسی در این باره را آغاز کرده‌اند.

news.originalContent:

The Nets have been a bottom five team in the NBA this season from the free-throw line, and they certainly left too many points at the stripe in Monday’s loss to the 76ers.

The Nets shot just 22-for-34 for a 64.7 percent conversion rate in their 12-point defeat. For the season, Brooklyn is ranked 26th in the league at 74.8 percent through its 3-10 start.

“Once again, I don’t want to go to the players and be like, ‘We gotta make free throws,’ because then you go there and you’re nervous,” Nets coach Jordi Fernández said.

“Obviously I don’t want to shoot 64 percent. … If we shoot better, we probably have a bigger chance. But I know our guys are good shooters and they’re gonna make free throws. We gotta concentrate and make sure that we believe that all of them are going to go in.”

Nolan Traore, Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle were a combined 19-for-21 from the line, but Egor Dëmin, Day’Ron Sharpe, Moritz Wagner and Danny Wolf combined to miss nine of 10 attempts.

Randle cut his lip in a face-to-face collision in Monday’s fourth quarter with Philly’s Jaylen Brown, who temporarily left the game to get his face bandaged. Brown also suffered a hamstring injury after returning to the floor.

“I’m fine. It feels terrible, to be honest. But I’m fine,” Randle said. “I just went to trap him and he turned, and he didn’t see me. Just kind of collided, but it’s fine.”

NBA legend Julius “Dr. J” Erving and former Nets coach Kevin Loughery will highlight the alumni present for a ceremony at halftime of Wednesday’s game against the Bulls honoring the Nets’ 1974 and 1976 ABA championship teams as part of the franchise’s 60th season.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Matisse Thybulle’s explanation for how he steals passes midair while opponents try to get the ball up the court is simple.

Even if the act of stealing the pass like a free safety intercepts a quarterback isn’t.

“I just look at the person passing; I just make eye contact with them,” Thybulle said after Tuesday’s shootaround ahead of the Lakers’ home game against the Hornets. “Because most guys aren’t really throwing no-look passes. Like Luka [Dončić], [Nikola] Jokić, there’s a couple guys in the league who really throw nowhere passes, especially in transition.

“So if you just look people in their eyes, they’re going to look where they’re throwing the ball. I can just get a sense from the eye contact.”

But if everyone was able to pick off passes like Thybulle, who’s shown a knack for playing the passing lanes throughout his eight-year NBA career, then they would.

So what makes him more equipped at picking off passes in a way that looks easy?

“Just being willing to take the risk,” he said. “I’ve missed a bunch of gambles as well as getting some. So just being willing to take the risk of assuming that where they’re looking is in fact where the guy is trying to pass the ball to.”

The Lakers have benefited from the defensive gambles the 6-foot-5 wing takes.

They entered Tuesday leading the league in defensive turnover percentage (18.7), according to Cleaning The Glass, and Thybulle is a significant reason.

He entered Tuesday ranked No. 2 in the league in total steals (31) and deflections (60).

“Me and [assistant] coach Greg [St. Jean] have talked a lot about that — just trying to find ways for me to be me within the foundation of our defense,” Thybulle said. “And they like me gambling because it generates turnovers, whether I’m getting the steal. It’s just a matter of doing it in ways where our defense can absorb the mistake, if you will. If I do it in ways where our defense is structured to be able to absorb it, then it’s something that we can just use, and I try to use to give us an advantage.”

The Lakers empowering Thybulle to take advantage of his defensive freedom, similar to how Dončić takes advantage of his offensive freedom, goes back to trust that was established during the preseason and training camp.

“It can be challenging at times to play with someone like me who’s taking a lot of risks, gambling, getting out of position and sometimes throwing off the team defense,” he said. “And it can be really easy for them to just be like, ‘Well, Matisse keeps messing up our defense. Like, what the hell is he doing?’ But they understand and they let me learn from my mistakes.”

He continued: “I gamble and sometimes I don’t get the pass, but sometimes I get a steal on the back end. There’s just the rapport that’s grown through that.”

news.originalContent:

Mater Dei announced on Tuesday that two-year head coach Raul Lara will no longer coach the school’s football program.

According to Steve Fryer of The Orange County Register, the school “described the parting as a mutual agreement” between the two sides.

“Mater Dei High School announces the departure of Raul Lara as head football coach. Lara joined Mater Dei in 2024 and led the Monarchs to an undefeated 13-0 season, capturing Trinity League, CIF Southern Section Division 1, CIF State Open Division and National Championships in his first season,” the school said in a statement.

“We thank Coach Lara for his service to Mater Dei High School and his contributions to our football program. We wish him the best in future endeavors,” said President Michael Brennan in the statement.

In Lara’s place, Randy Wright has been appointed as the school’s interim head coach while they begin searching for a new leader of the historic football program.

Mater Dei, the only high school to produce three Heisman Trophy winners in the country, came crashing to Earth two years after the undefeated season. Nevertheless, it appears the expectations are sky high.

Lara’s departure comes after the school finished with an 8-3 record that included a 25-8 loss to Bishop Gorman from Nevada, while going 4-1 in the Trinity League with a 14-7 loss to reigning CIF Division 1 Champion, Santa Margarita.

Last Friday, the Monarchs were shockingly blown out of the water by Corona Centennial, losing 45-15 in a quarterfinals matchup of the CIF Southern Section Division 1 playoffs.

Fryer reported that Lara told Monarchs players of his departure on Tuesday morning.

Lara’s tenure with the Monarchs comes after he replaced Frank McManus, who coached there for only one year in 2023.

McManus came on the scene after they parted ways with Bruce Rollinson, who coached at the school for 33 years from 1989 to 2022.

Through their trying year, Mater Dei rotated between three different quarterbacks last season and eventually stuck with freshman Paytyn Guess.

According to MaxPreps, Guess played in 11 games this season and completed 73 of 125 passes for 1,108 yards with 10 touchdowns and four interceptions.

According to Fryer, Guess was replaced in Friday’s game against Centennial with senior Cameron Polley.

The Monarchs struggled to get their running game going, as they ran for just 20 yards on 34 attempts.

California could be staring down a weather catastrophe of historic proportions, with scientists warning that a hypothetical megastorm could unleash biblical flooding, hurricane-force winds and an astonishing $725 billion in economic damage.

The nightmare scenario, known as an ARkStorm, envisions weeks of relentless atmospheric rivers battering the Golden State, overwhelming flood defenses, swallowing entire communities and potentially forcing millions of residents to evacuate.

The frightening scenario, presented by the US Geological Survey, comes as back-to-back atmospheric rivers pound the West Coast, with another powerful Pacific storm targeting California and threatening heavy rainfall and several feet of snow in the Sierra Nevada, according to Fox Weather.

Scientists warn that the kind of megastorm envisioned in the ARkStorm model could make even a severe winter storm look tame.

news.originalContent:

WASHINGTON — Reality TV star Paris Hilton on Tuesday begged Republican House leaders to pass the DEFIANCE Act, pointing out that more than half the female members of Congress are victims of deepfake porn.

“Of the 156 women serving in the 119th Congress, 83 have sexual deepfakes online right now. That is more than half the women in Congress,” Hilton said at a press conference on Capitol Hill, surrounded by Democratic and Republican members of Congress.

It was the second trip to the Capitol this year for Hilton, the 45-year-old celebrity businesswoman who has become an advocate for the legislation, which combats non-consensual sexually explicit AI-generated deepfakes and digital forgeries.

“I will come back to these halls as many times as it takes until the Defiance Act is signed. Because the abuse hasn’t stopped, and neither will I,” she vowed.

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) and Rep. Laurel Lee (R-Fla.), co-sponsors of the legislation, joined Hilton in appealing to the GOP leadership to put the DEFIANCE Act on the House calendar.

Everyday the DEFIANCE Act isn’t signed into law “is a day that more children, women and people are victimized with no recourse,” AOC said.

“Thousands of people in this country, if not tens of thousands and eventually millions, could be subject to sexual abuse on our watch just due to complacency.”

Hilton had a one-on-one meeting with Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) on Tuesday as part of her lobbying effort but declined to tell reporters if he was receptive to her appeal.

In an impassioned plea, the Hilton hotels heiress addressed Johnson and other members of the GOP leadership directly: “I am speaking directly to you. Will you allow this to continue to happen to your colleagues? How about the women in your district? How about your daughters, your wives, or your sisters?”

The DEFIANCE Act has seen little movement in the House since being introduced in May 2025 despite having a range of bipartisan support.

That may be because of AOC and her future political ambitions. Republicans, who still control the House, are reluctant to hand the Democratic firebrand a major legislative victory, particularly as she mulls a 2028 presidential bid.

“This is a bipartisan bill that enjoys broad support among the Republican and Democratic caucuses, and it is an amazing opportunity for us to unify as a country for the protection of women, girls, and people everywhere. We can do this. And survivors cannot wait,” Ocasio-Cortez said.

The legislation has passed the Senate unanimously but, if the House doesn’t approve it before this legislative session ends on Jan. 3, the DEFIANCE Act will have to start the legislative process all over again.

The legislation protects everyone, Hilton noted.

“This is not a Republican or Democratic issue. This is a human issue,” she said. “Our likeness is not your content. Our trauma is not your entertainment. And our consent is never optional.”

The DEFIANCE Act sounds similar to the Take It Down Act, the legislation championed by Melania Trump and signed into law by President Trump in May.

But the two work in conjunction, covering criminal and civil penalties.

The Take It Down Act implemented criminal measures for those who threatened or knowingly published deepfake pornography. It also requires social media companies and online apps to establish “report and remove” mechanisms and delete non-consensual sexual images within 48 hours of a report.

Hilton’s DEFIANCE Act creates a civil path for victims to directly sue individuals in court for monetary damages.

The actress and reality star has spoken of the harassment and humiliation she experienced when she was 19 and her ex-boyfriend published an explicit sex tape featuring her without her consent.

Hilton never saw any profits from the video posted by her ex and said she donated her $400,000 settlement with him to charity.

“I will keep showing up, speaking out, and fighting for every survivor who deserves justice, dignity, and control over their own likeness,” Hilton told The Post on Monday.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Former St. John’s star RJ Luis Jr is on LSU’s roster after all — for now, at least — in the latest twist to a months-long eligibility saga.

Luis, the 2024-25 Big East Player of the Year who inked a two-way deal with the Jazz and an Exhibit 10 contract with the Celtics, committed to LSU in May but wasn’t eligible to play after signing an NBA contract.

But after receiving a preliminary injunction from a Louisiana judge and after the SEC said it wouldn’t punish the school to roster Luis, according to ESPN, the Tigers officially added him Tuesday — though it’s unclear if Luis would play as soon as Wednesday, when LSU hosts Louisiana Monroe.

“RJ secured his eligibility through a court order before the new SEC policy interpretation was announced,” LSU President Wade Rousse said in a statement Tuesday, where he announced the university’s intention to roster Luis. “He went to court when he believed the NCAA had violated his rights. After a full evidentiary hearing, the Court ruled in his favor and enjoined the NCAA from declaring or treating him as ineligible. Neither the appellate court nor the Louisiana Supreme Court has disturbed that ruling. Under the SEC rules at the time, that ruling made him eligible to compete in the SEC as well.”

After averaging 18.2 points and 7.2 rebounds per game during his final season under Rick Pitino, Luis signed a two-way deal with the Jazz and then an Exhibit 10 deal with the Celtics ahead of the 2025-26 season.

He never appeared in a G League game or NBA regular-season game, but he did appear in three preseason contests last year.

On the LSU roster, Luis was listed as No. 12 — the same number he wore with St. John’s and during his preseason cameos with Boston.

In the latest injunction, the judge ruled that the SEC — as well as commissioner Greg Sankey — and the NCAA couldn’t punish the Tigers if they had Luis on the roster, according to On3.com.

“LSU signed RJ in May 2026,” Rousse said in his statement Tuesday. “He is a full-time LSU student. He went to court when he believed the NCAA had violated his rights. After a full evidentiary hearing, the Court ruled in his favor and enjoined the NCAA from declaring or treating him as ineligible. Neither the appellate court nor the Louisiana Supreme Court has disturbed that ruling. Under the SEC rules at the time, that ruling made him eligible to compete in the SEC as well.

“The day after that ruling was issued, the SEC announced its more aggressive interpretation of the eligibility rules with program-ending penalties for violations.”

LSU, with head coach Will Wade returning to the program for a second stint, has opened the season 4-0 — including a one-point victory over No. 14 Gonzaga on Saturday — and was ranked No. 25 in the most recent Associated Press Top 25 poll.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Hedge fund billionaire Ken Griffin has sold a sprawling Park Avenue duplex to New York Jets owner Woody Johnson for $58 million — just months after Mayor Zohran Mamdani targeted the Citadel founder in a creepy video touting the lefty’s new pied-à-terre tax.

Johnson, an heir to the Johnson & Johnson fortune, snapped up the roughly 8,500-square-foot residence at 740 Park Ave., one of the Upper East Side’s most exclusive addresses, in an off-market deal.

Griffin bought the two-floor spread for $45 million in 2025 from Julia Koch, the widow of billionaire industrialist David Koch.

The new transaction represents a roughly 29% increase over Griffin’s purchase price, before accounting for any transaction costs or improvements. Griffin paid $13 million less for the pad just last year.

“I wish Woody and his family many happy years in one of New York’s great residences,” Griffin told The Post on Tuesday.

The sale comes after the billionaire clashed publicly with Mamdani over the democratic socialist’s push to tax the city’s wealthiest property owners.

In April, Mamdani filmed a Tax Day video outside Griffin’s $238 million penthouse at 220 Central Park South, which the hedge fund mogul purchased in 2019 in what was then the most expensive residential real estate transaction in US history.

The mayor singled out Griffin’s apartment while promoting a proposed tax on luxury second homes valued at $5 million or more.

Griffin blasted the stunt as a “personal attack” and a “profound lack of judgment,” while Citadel subsequently raised questions about its planned multibillion-dollar office tower at 350 Park Ave.

Speaking at the Milken Institute Global Conference in May, Griffin said the tower remained “a point of discussion internally” and that his firm needed to “double down on our bet in Miami.”

The Park Avenue duplex, which was previously marketed with five bedrooms, was never publicly listed for sale. Few details about its interior finishes have been disclosed.

The purchase gives Johnson, the former US ambassador to Britain, a new foothold in Manhattan’s ultra-exclusive co-op market more than a decade after he sold his duplex at nearby 834 Fifth Ave. to billionaire Leonard Blavatnik for $77.5 million.

Johnson also owns a sprawling estate in Bedminster, NJ, which he originally purchased for $3.3 million in 1984, as well as a Palm Beach, Fla., residence acquired in 2020 for approximately $33 million.

The limestone building at 740 Park Ave., developed around 1930 by real estate investor James T. Lee, the grandfather of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, contains roughly 30 apartments.

It has continued to command eye-popping prices despite softer demand for luxury Manhattan co-ops.

Despite unloading his latest Park Avenue property, Griffin isn’t abandoning the prestigious address.

The Citadel boss still owns an adjacent apartment at 740 Park Ave. that he purchased earlier this year for $38 million, according to the Journal.

Ryan Serhant and Melissa Post of Serhant represented Johnson in the transaction.

As for the pied-à-terre tax, New York City is poised to mail bills to about 7,500 homeowners — raising questions about the controversial policy’s ballyhooed revenue potential, as The Post reported.

The Post has sought comment from Johnson.

Palm Beach’s “fake Cartier heiress” Andrea Bartzen is in NYC and being turned away at parties.

Bartzen — who was the subject of a scathing NY Mag article that claimed she stiffed bills and made up her lineage to infiltrate elite circles  — was spotted attempting and failing to get into a 25th anniversary bash for high-end chocolatier MarieBelle on Monday night.

“She was trying to convince the publicist to let her in,” says a source at the party at the Broome Street store. “They wouldn’t let her in.”

The event was thrown by longtime PR guru Norah Lawlor.

Lawlor is based in NYC, but spends her winters in Palm Beach where she throws events and handles clients like real heiress Consuelo Vanderbilt Costin.

“Andrea showed up,” Lawlor told us when we called to ask about what happened. “She wasn’t on the guest list, she wasn’t invited.”

Bartzen, while failing to sweet-talk her way in to the treat shop, didn’t leave empty-handed.

“I gave her a goodie bag,” Lawlor told us. “She asked to come back later and I said, ‘No. You are not on the list. I will invite you one day when it’s appropriate.'”

Lawlor told us, “Don’t go if you’re not invited. That’s the rules.”

And while that is how the artisanal cookie crumbled, this could all be a big misunderstanding.

Bartzen says she was invited by another guest as a plus-one, which Page Six has confirmed. The guest, however, never got it approved.

“I went to have a business meeting with someone there who was invited,” she told us. “I said please add me as a plus-one and get it confirmed … Norah, the gatekeeper, said ‘You didn’t RSVP personally,’ and so I said ‘Fine’ and didn’t go to the event.”

“The girl that invited me stepped outside, we had a five-minute meeting and then I left,” Bartzen tells us.

Bartzen then threatened to sue us multiple times and accused us of “assault journalism.”

news.originalContent:
Iran claims drone strike on US radar was retaliation for alleged airspace violations by US military drones.

Kuwait’s army has said the Gulf country is under attack by drones while the United States and Iran traded blows, marking escalating tensions in the region as a peace deal remains elusive.

The military said in a statement on X on Tuesday that “any explosion sounds heard are the result of air defence systems intercepting hostile attacks”.

The US earlier carried out several attacks on Iran’s southern island of Qeshm, in the Strait of Hormuz, hours after Iran said it launched a drone attack on a US radar system in Bahrain.

“The American attack on locations on Qeshm island caused no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas,” Ahmad Nafisi, deputy governor of Iran’s southern Hormozgan province, told the official IRNA news agency on Tuesday.

He said the situation was under control and relief agencies were on full alert. IRNA reported five to six explosions on the island on Tuesday evening.

A US official told Al Jazeera the strike hit a missile launch site on Qeshm, in response to Iran’s earlier attack on a US base in Bahrain.

US Central Command said Iranian drones aimed at a US radar system at an air base in Bahrain “were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or personnel”.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it carried out a “precision operation” with drones on the US-operated radar at the Sheikh Isa air base, in response to “repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones”.

Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, said its air defences intercepted the attack, and blasts were heard over the capital, Manama, according to the AFP news agency.

It was the third Iranian drone attack on Bahrain in five days after a lull of several weeks. Friday’s strike was the first Iranian attack on a Gulf country since early September, AFP reported. Reuters said it came after a Bahraini court sentenced 64 people, mostly Shia clerics, to life in prison for allegedly colluding with Iran.

Kuwait’s armed forces said on Tuesday night that its air defences were responding to “hostile drone attacks” and urged the public to follow safety instructions.

It did not say where the drones came from or whether there were casualties or damage.

Iran’s armed forces said three oil tankers struck naval mines while trying to cross the strait on Tuesday. The US military says it cleared the main routes of mines.

Since the war began on February 28, Iran has tried to restrict traffic through the strait, which normally carries about a fifth of the world’s oil, insisting that ships use only routes it has authorised. The US has responded with a naval blockade of Iranian ports and has escorted tankers.

Another tanker, the Panamanian-flagged Tara Gas, was struck on Monday about seven nautical miles north of Khasab, in Oman, causing a fire in its engine room, according to the security firm Vanguard.

Vanguard and India’s ports minister initially said all 25 crew, 24 of them Indian, were safe. But the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said the vessel was hit a second time and the crew were “currently unaccounted for”. India’s ports minister later said the crew had abandoned the vessel after a second attack and that one Indian sailor was missing. Another Panamanian-flagged tanker, the On Phoenix, was hit by an unidentified projectile off Oman’s coast on Monday.

Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, and his Omani counterpart, Badr Albusaidi, discussed safeguarding shipping and diplomatic options in Muscat, Oman’s news agencies said.

A third US aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, arrived in the Middle East on Monday, and US President Donald Trump is due to hold a three-way summit on Thursday in China with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, where the Iran war is on the agenda.

news.originalContent:
Eisenkot’s bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu’s most contentious policies following Kahana’s election.

Israeli lawmakers have elected Matan Kahana as the new parliament speaker, marking a step towards reversing domestic policies from the outgoing government led by Benjamin Netanyahu.

Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot – the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Netanyahu – was voted in on Tuesday, receiving 66 votes in the 120-member chamber.

Netanyahu’s Likud party had put forward Ofir Katz as its own candidate. He received 52 votes following a stormy debate that stretched over seven hours.

The Israel parliament speaker is an important office given that it sets the timetable for parliamentary business and can therefore speed up or delay debates or votes on proposed legislation.

“I will be a Knesset speaker for everyone, irrespective of race, religion or gender,” said Kahana during his inauguration speech immediately after the vote.

Kahana, a 54-year-old former special forces soldier, is expected as soon as Wednesday to start the process of undoing much of Netanyahu’s domestic agenda, especially regarding contentious reforms to the judiciary.

Netanyahu is Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, having been in and out of office for three decades.

The vote took place weeks after October 27 parliamentary elections in which neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu won a majority in the Knesset, with the two blocs trading barbs since then.

Eisenkot’s wide-ranging bloc secured 48 seats, while Netanyahu’s finished with 53. Two Arab-majority slates won an unprecedented 19 seats on the back of anger over Netanyahu’s hard-right government.

On Tuesday, the two lists voted for Eisenkot’s candidate Kahana as parliament speaker, with one Arab Knesset member absent.

Netanyahu’s and Eisenkot’s parties met on Sunday to discuss the possibility of joining a unity government but the meeting appeared to be largely a formality, with both men saying they should be prime minister.

Netanyahu, who has reportedly been urging US President Donald Trump to resume the war on Iran, has talked up the threat from Tehran as he insists on the need for a unity government.

With Kahana at the helm and if Eisenkot retains the backing of the Arab-Israeli parties, he has an opportunity to deal serious blows to Netanyahu’s legislative agenda even before a possible government is formed.

Eisenkot has said he wants to rescind sweeping reforms to reduce the independence of the judiciary that were advanced by Netanyahu, who has been enraged over corruption charges against him that could land him in prison if he loses power.

Eisenkot has also vowed to quickly set up a state commission of inquiry to investigate security failures that led to Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack.

Netanyahu, who has built his brand on saying he will ensure Israel’s security, has refused an independent probe, instead proposing one whose members would be chosen by politicians.

Kahana, who is now a member of Eisenkot’s Yashar party, served in a short-lived non-Netanyahu government in 2021 and 2022 as minister for religious services, during which he clashed with ultra-Orthodox Jews by seeking to reduce the power of the Chief Rabbinate.

Kahana himself is an observant Jew, part of Eisenkot’s efforts to form a broad coalition that ranges from secular liberals to religious conservatives.

As parliament speaker, Kahana succeeds Amir Ohana, a Netanyahu ally who has held the position since 2022.
